title: bd dolt push fails 403: sync.remote points at upstream, not the fork
description: 'bd dolt push' fails with 'fatal: unable to access https://github.com/noshishiRust/leptos-daisyui-rs.git/: The requested URL returned error: 403'. Cause: .beads/config.yaml line 64 sets sync.remote to git+https://github.com/noshishiRust/leptos-daisyui-rs.git -- that is UPSTREAM (noshishiRust), which we have no write access to. This repo is an internal fork; the writable remote is 'fork' = https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git. Consequence: beads state is not being backed up off-machine. Confirmed .beads/issues.jsonl is stale (23 issues, all closed, missing ldui-b08), so recent closures live only in the local Dolt DB and would be lost with the workstation. Not auto-fixed: repointing sync.remote decides where issue data gets published, which is a human call. Fix candidates: (a) bd config set sync.remote git+https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git then bd dolt push; or (b) rely on the git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl and get auto-flush/export working so closures land in commits.
acceptance_criteria: bd dolt push exits 0, OR .beads/issues.jsonl contains ldui-b08 as closed and is committed to the fork.
notes: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED. Not sync.remote in config.yaml -- 'bd dolt push' never reads that key. The real setting is the DOLT remote: 'bd dolt remote list' showed origin -> git+https://github.com/noshishiRust/leptos-daisyui-rs.git (upstream, unwritable). Repointing sync.remote to the fork changed 'bd config get sync.remote' but the very next push still 403'd against upstream, which is what exposed the mistake. Fix applied: bd dolt remote remove origin; bd dolt remote add origin git+https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git. Verified both the SQL-side view (bd dolt remote list) and the CLI-side view (dolt remote -v in .beads/dolt/ldui) agree, then 'bd dolt push' returned 'Push complete.' (exit 0). sync.remote was also left pointing at the fork -- harmless and directionally right. NOTE: 'bd dolt remote add' warns it only writes the SQL side; check the CLI side too. STILL OPEN and NOT fixed by this: .beads/issues.jsonl is stale (23 issues, all closed, missing ldui-b08), so the git-tracked JSONL export is not keeping up with the Dolt DB. Tracked separately in ldui-2ux.
close_reason: Fixed: the Dolt remote 'origin' pointed at upstream noshishiRust (unwritable). Removed and re-added it as git+https://github.com/davidcforbes/leptos-daisyui-rs.git; verified SQL-side and CLI-side views agree; 'bd dolt push' now returns 'Push complete.' (exit 0). The title's blame on sync.remote was wrong -- see notes. Residual stale-JSONL issue split out to ldui-izn.

title: Keep EntityTable column filters reachable in compact and hidden-column layouts
description: EntityTable renders controlled column filters only in the desktop thead, which is hidden below the lg breakpoint. It also omits a filter control when its column is hidden through the chooser. Office No-Hires and the operational satellite wave therefore lose the only direct editor for an active filter in compact layouts or after hiding a filtered column. A page-level Reset may exist, but EntityColumnFilter currently carries only a column ID and renderer, so the framework cannot disclose or clear hidden active filters.
design: Keep filter values and matching logic consumer-controlled. Add enough typed filter presentation metadata, such as localized label, active state, and clear intent, to render one responsive fallback in the table toolbar or a compact filter panel. Do not render duplicate focusable controls at the same breakpoint, and do not make column visibility own domain filter state.
acceptance_criteria: Desktop aligned filters retain the light-blue second header row. Below the desktop breakpoint every supplied filter remains reachable, labelled, keyboard operable, and tied to the same controlled value. Hiding a column with an active filter leaves that filter visible and removable or clearly blocks the hide operation. Restoring a column does not duplicate or reset its filter. Active hidden filters are announced in table presentation. Browser coverage exercises compact layout, a hidden filtered column, localization, Reset, and restoration without duplicate control IDs or stale rows.
close_reason: Completed

title: Add controlled query ownership to ServerDataTable
description: ServerDataTable emits TableQuery but privately owns search, sort, and column-filter signals. A consumer cannot restore route or saved state, apply a server-normalized query, clear all table controls from the opinionated FilterBar Reset action, or atomically reset query state when a dataset changes. This risks visible controls disagreeing with the request that produced the displayed slice.
design: Add an explicit controlled or uncontrolled query-ownership model analogous to EntityTable preference ownership. One typed query value should drive visible search, sort metadata, filters, page size, and paging strategy; callbacks remain transport-neutral.
acceptance_criteria: A controlled caller supplies the query currently represented by the displayed rows and receives one proposed query per user transition; externally replacing or resetting the query updates every visible control and aria-sort without a feedback loop; declined or delayed proposals restore the supplied DOM value; dataset and access generation changes cannot retain stale query state; uncontrolled legacy behavior remains source-compatible; native and browser negative controls cover Reset, server normalization, locale change, and rejected updates.

title: Support cursor pagination in ServerDataTable without invented totals
description: Office Conversations is keyset-paged and returns opaque next cursors with no population total. ServerDataTable requires current_page, total_count, page_size, and offset navigation, so the page sets total_count to zero, disables on_page_change, and renders a second custom pager. Add a typed cursor or keyset paging strategy so server-owned tables can represent this API truthfully.
design: Model offset and cursor paging as explicit mutually exclusive strategies. Cursor tokens remain opaque caller-owned transport values; the table owns only presentation and emits typed navigation intent. Search, sort, and filter changes must restart from the first cursor generation.
acceptance_criteria: ServerDataTable can render a current server slice with previous and next availability and no total or fabricated page number; Previous and Next emit typed cursor navigation exactly once; search, sort, filter, and page-size changes reset cursor navigation coherently; retained loading and failed fetches keep the displayed slice truthfully labelled; existing offset callers remain source-compatible; browser coverage proves both strategies and rejects mixed offset/cursor configuration.

title: Add viewport-fit paging to EntityTable
description: Office standalone pages use a full-height shell, but EntityTable exposes only persisted fixed page sizes 25, 50, and 100. Unlike compatibility DataTable, it has no typed viewport-fit mode, so No-Hires cannot make its visible row count follow browser height without a page-local ResizeObserver and synthetic preference writes. Add an opt-in framework-owned fit policy while retaining the existing fixed-size API.
design: Treat viewport-derived row capacity as presentation state, not a persisted user preference. Reuse the measured-header and row-height mechanics already proven by DataTable where possible, and keep the complete client snapshot authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can enable viewport-fit paging with a definite-height container or maximum height; header, filter row, toolbar, pager, and measured row height contribute to capacity; resizing the browser, changing density, hiding columns, or changing localized copy recomputes without a reload; short viewports fall back safely; derived capacity is not persisted as page preference; fixed 25/50/100 behavior stays source-compatible; focused native and browser negative controls prove no clipping, nested vertical scrolling, oscillation, or stale page index.

title: Close invariant gaps in SnapshotTable foundation design before implementation
description:
## Context

This is the requested consumer review of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-snapshot-table-opinionated-foundation-design.md` at WDO commit `f39f541`, checked against `Future-Architecture.md` and the current `FilterSchema`, `EntityTable`, and `DataTable` APIs.

The overall direction is correct: keep transport and domain policy in consumers, make dataset replacement atomic, retain old content while a replacement loads, centralize page-state/action feedback, and keep the composition explicit Rust rather than a page generator. The following public-contract gaps should be resolved in the design before the foundation is implemented or frozen for consumers.

## Priority findings

1. **The proposed page slots do not enforce selector/table identity coherence.** The design says `SnapshotTablePage` accepts already-built `DatasetSelector`, `FilterBar`, and `EntityTable` slots, while also claiming the page derives selector presentation, table dataset identity, and rows from one `DatasetPresentation`. An opaque child can still bind unrelated signals and reproduce the original defect: new selector identity over old rows. Specify context-bound render closures or typed slot/config inputs that receive only a framework-derived read-only snapshot view. The canonical API must make a mismatched selector/table dataset identity impossible or explicitly detectable; documentation alone is not enforcement.

2. **The public orthogonal state shape permits contradictory combinations.** Independent public `dataset`, `content`, `access`, and `action` fields allow states such as `NeverLoaded + Ready`, a non-empty snapshot labeled `EmptyDataset`, or content derived from a previous revision paired with a newly displayed snapshot. Preserve legitimate orthogonality, but use private fields plus constructors/reducer transitions, and derive content from the displayed snapshot and current local-result count (or bind it to the displayed dataset identity/revision). Access replacement precedence must also be encoded rather than left to consumers assembling the struct.

3. **Caller-issued request tokens weaken the promised race guarantee.** A consumer can reuse or decrease the supposedly monotonic token; then a stale response can again match the active token and dataset identity. The pure transition model can deterministically mint its own opaque sequence token without using wall-clock time. At minimum, `start_request` must reject non-increasing/reused tokens and return the accepted opaque request handle used by completion/failure methods.

4. **A singular `ActionFeedbackState<K>` conflicts with keyed concurrent row actions.** “Idle or one keyed outcome” cannot represent two pending row mutations, or a pending mutation alongside a preference/action conflict, although the design says pending disables only the corresponding action. Either declare and enforce one in-flight page action, or model keyed concurrent action state (for example a keyed collection plus one latest live-region announcement). The chosen concurrency and dismissal/retry semantics need to be explicit.

5. **Reactive behavioral columns can leave the current sort cache stale.** `SortedIndexCache` currently keys reuse only by `Rc` row identity and `EntitySort`; it does not include column definitions. The design promises that reactive columns use the latest comparator/sort-key callbacks. If those callbacks change while rows and sort remain unchanged, the visible order incorrectly reuses old indices. Either keep behavioral column definitions stable and make only localized presentation text reactive, or add a stable column-definition revision/fingerprint to cache invalidation and reconcile removed/non-sortable sort IDs. Apply the same presentation/behavior split to compact rendering.

6. **`SnapshotViewDefaults<F>` does not exclude dataset identity “by construction” when `F` is arbitrary.** Current `FilterSchema<T>` stores `PhantomData<T>` and validates only declared string keys; it cannot prevent a consumer-defined serializable `F` from containing `office_id` or another dataset selector. Use a framework-owned schema-keyed filter payload, a sealed/validated projection that serializes only schema-declared fields, or narrow the claim and add runtime validation. Include a negative compile/runtime fixture whose consumer filter type attempts to carry dataset identity.

7. **The sortable-header accessibility contract is incomplete.** The design gives the nested sort control only the localized column header as its accessible name and keeps `aria-sort` on the parent `th`. The existing `ldui-w1e` acceptance requires the focused control to expose current sort state. Define localized current-state and next-action text (including multi-sort position where applicable) and expose it directly to the focusable control or via an explicitly associated description; do not rely on assistive technology inferring the parent header state.

8. **Focus recovery needs a dataset/generation boundary and eligibility rule.** “If the row disappears from the supplied dataset” also occurs during dataset replacement, access replacement, filtering, or wholesale refresh. The table must not move focus from a removed row into an unrelated row in a newly selected dataset. Reset/suppress row-action recovery across dataset identity generations and access replacement; for an in-dataset removal, target the same action only when it remains rendered, enabled, and focusable, otherwise use the named table-region fallback. State what happens when filtering/paging hides the focused row without deleting it.

These are design corrections, not a request to broaden the consumer MVP or introduce framework transport/persistence.
design:
## Recommended resolution

- Introduce a framework-derived `SnapshotTableView` (name illustrative) containing displayed/requested identity, displayed rows/revision/count, transition kind, and valid panel state. Pass this value into selector/table render closures or typed configs owned by `SnapshotTablePage`.
- Keep the state machine pure and deterministic: it owns the next request sequence and returns an opaque request handle; completion and failure consume/check that handle plus dataset identity.
- Keep orthogonal axes internally, but expose only validated constructors and reducer operations. Bind any derived content result to the displayed snapshot revision.
- Decide whether actions are serialized or concurrent and encode that choice in the type. If concurrent, separate keyed operational state from the single announcement chosen for the live region.
- Split reactive column presentation from stable sorting/cell behavior, or introduce an explicit semantic column revision that invalidates `SortedIndexCache` and normalizes preferences/sort clauses.
- Replace arbitrary persisted `F` with a schema-projected payload, or require an explicit projection callback whose output can contain only validated local-filter keys.
- Add localized sort-state/next-action strings to the shared table text contract and specify the focused control's computed accessible name/description.
- Include dataset identity/generation in the focus record, clear it on replacement/access transitions, and verify target focusability before moving focus.

Update `ldui-ifj.1`, `ldui-ifj.2`, `ldui-ifj.3`, and `ldui-w1e` acceptance language as needed so implementation cannot satisfy the children while leaving these contradictions unresolved.
acceptance_criteria: The design, implementation plan, Future-Architecture, and affected Beads are revised before implementation freeze. Canonical configs cannot wire selector identity, displayed rows, and table identity from unrelated sources; contradictory state is unconstructable; request handles are framework-issued/non-reusable; concurrent keyed actions and one latest announcement are encoded; semantic column generation invalidates stale sort caches; schema-projected defaults reject dataset identity; focused sort controls expose localized current/next copy; focus never crosses dataset/access generations or targets ineligible actions. The approved aligned-filter, semantic blue/faint-grid, opt-in-zebra, and sort-stable geometry contracts are explicit, with named negative fixtures for every invariant.
close_reason: Reviewed invariants and owner decisions are represented in the governing architecture, design spec, implementation plan, and affected Bead acceptance criteria.

title: Add typed SnapshotTablePage, PageStatePanel, and ActionFeedback patterns
description: Implement the adopted Layer 2 and Layer 3 snapshot-page building blocks as typed composition, not a page generator. A private-field SnapshotTableState mints opaque request handles, atomically owns displayed snapshot/access state, derives generation-bound read-only views, and holds keyed concurrent action feedback. SnapshotTablePage renders identity-critical DatasetSelector and EntityTable bindings itself from typed configs that cannot supply unrelated selected/displayed identity or rows. Domain columns, filter values, mutation transport, persistence, routes, and page-safe content remain caller-owned.
acceptance_criteria: Request handles are framework-issued, strictly increasing, consumed, and non-constructible by callers; stale/duplicate/mismatched completions cannot change any displayed field. Contradictory dataset/content/access states are unconstructable, local-result summaries are accepted only for the displayed generation/revision, and expired/forbidden access cannot retain actionable bindings. Switching datasets retains and labels the displayed snapshot, exposes the requested destination, then atomically swaps rows/revision/count/identity; failure retains old data with Retry. Canonical typed selector/table configs have no identity/row fields, and browser generation markers agree. Keyed action state supports concurrent distinct pending entries while one latest transition owns the live announcement; Retry/Dismiss affect only their key. Focused native/browser break-and-revert controls pass.
close_reason: Completed typed SnapshotTablePage foundation with opaque checked request/action state, typed identity-coherent composition, action/state panels, documentation, focused reducer tests, and real-browser negative controls; cargo xtask verify passed 14/14.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Read-only review of the current dirty TDD checkpoint found four reducer-level gaps before rendering: (1) SnapshotTableState::set_action has no access or generation guard, so a stale completion after replace_access(Expired) can repopulate actions, and an atomic dataset swap retains old-dataset action entries. Bind action transitions to framework-issued generation/key context or reject stale and access-unavailable transitions. (2) ActionFeedbackModel::dismiss removes an entry but leaves latest_announcement pointing to the dismissed key. (3) complete on a dataset mismatch leaves active_request intact even though the supplied handle was consumed, trapping the phase in InitialLoading/Replacing unless a caller cloned the handle or starts another request; make the mismatch a terminal typed transition. (4) public SnapshotRenderDecision constructors and Default for SnapshotGeneration let consumers fabricate values described as derived and opaque. Keep construction framework-private. Focused reducer cases are sufficient at this stage.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Completion evidence: resolved all four reducer review gaps with focused tests. Action transitions now require framework-issued generation/key/sequence handles, reject stale or access-unavailable completions, and are cleared on dataset/access replacement. Dismiss clears the latest announcement. Dataset-mismatch completion consumes and terminates the active request without trapping InitialLoading/Replacing. title: data_table auto-rows measure timer fires after unmount — disposed-signal panic
description:
component.rs:802: schedule_measure() runs set_timeout_with_handle(measure_rows, Duration::ZERO) and DISCARDS the TimeoutHandle, so nothing can cancel it. The auto-page Effect (~component.rs:816, deps: auto_page_size/table_size/data/page_size) schedules it on mount and on every data change; the ResizeObserver callback schedules it too. measure_rows then calls auto_rows.get_untracked() and auto_rows.set(...) with NO disposed-guard.

If the host app navigates away inside that zero-delay macrotask window, the timer fires after the DataTable's reactive owner is disposed and the whole wasm app panics: reactive_graph traits.rs:361 'Tried to access a reactive value that has already been disposed.'

Repro: any router navigation immediately after a DataTable (auto_page_size or not — the measure Effect always runs) mounts or re-renders; caught deterministically by 4iiz-etl's PixelProof visual gate (bead bd_4iiz-etl-rnn.24) on its History→Errors transition. The gate currently paces navigations ~150ms apart to drain the pending macrotask — a workaround, not a fix.

Fix: (1) store the TimeoutHandle (the search debounce at component.rs:421/:445 already models exactly this — keep the two consistent) and clear it in on_cleanup; (2) belt-and-braces: measure_rows should use try-forms (auto_rows.try_with_untracked / try_set) so a late callback degrades to a no-op instead of a process-wide panic. ServerDataTable's debounce keeps its handle but is never cleared on cleanup either — same pass should cover it.
close_reason: All three timer-outlives-owner sites fixed and merged to main (4e22e34): measure timer handle stored/cancelled on reschedule and on_cleanup with try-form guards in measure_rows; client search debounce try-sets and cancels on unmount; ServerDataTable debounce entry-guarded and cancelled on unmount. Regression test data_table_timers_survive_unmount arms all three timers and navigates in the same task — it captured two disposed-signal panics before the fix, green after; full reactivity suite 25/25, clippy clean, 2273 lib tests green. 4iiz-etl (bd_4iiz-etl-rnn.24) can drop the 150ms navigation pacing workaround.

comments.text: Second site, same class (found by the same 4iiz-etl gate run once navigations were paced past the ZERO-delay measure timer): server_component.rs:259/:319 — ServerDataTable's 300ms search debounce stores its TimeoutHandle in a signal but NEVER cancels it in on_cleanup. When it fires after the table's owner is disposed, the closure's emit_query(1) untracked-reads page_size/sort state on disposed signals -> the same reactive_graph traits.rs:361 panic. component.rs:421/:445 (plain DataTable's debounce) shares the shape. Fix family for all three timers: cancel the handle in on_cleanup AND make the callbacks use try_ forms so a late fire degrades to a no-op. The consuming gate currently paces navigations 500ms apart (> the longest timer) as a workaround.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text: Third site, same class, and the one no consumer-side pacing can dodge: the ResizeObserver attached at component.rs:840-868. When SPA navigation removes the table wrapper from the DOM, the observer can deliver a size-change callback IN THE SAME TASK as the unmount; the callback runs schedule_measure/measure_rows against the just-disposed owner -> the same reactive_graph disposal panic, and a wasm panic poisons the whole instance. on_cleanup's disconnect() runs during reactive teardown, which can be AFTER the delivery is already queued for that task. title: A failed Tailwind build leaves trunk serving a STALE output.css, and both browser audit suites pass green against it
description: Found 2026-08-10 while landing ldui-vh6. A syntax error in demo/input.css (a comment quoting a glob ending in */ closed the comment early) made tailwindcss exit with CssSyntaxError. trunk carried on and kept serving the PREVIOUS output.css. Both browser suites then ran and PASSED against that stale stylesheet - cargo xtask test-style 7/7 and test-layout 9/9, with STYLE-EXIT=0. cargo xtask verify cannot see it either, because it runs cargo check and never invokes trunk. CONSEQUENCE: the entire computed-style audit system - every ceiling, every ratchet, the whole point of ldui-9rf - can report green while measuring a stylesheet that failed to build. The suites are not testing the CSS you just wrote; they are testing whatever CSS last succeeded. This is strictly worse than the known 'npm install missing -> stale dist' trap already in the demo-trunk-build-prereqs memory, because that one fails loudly on first run while this one only bites after a previously-good build exists.
design: The audit harness must refuse to run against a stylesheet it cannot prove is current. Options: (a) have the xtask browser-suite steps run the tailwind build themselves and FAIL on a non-zero exit rather than delegating to trunk's pre_build hook, whose failure trunk swallows; (b) assert a freshness marker - stamp a build id into output.css and have harness_at verify the served stylesheet carries the id of the current input.css hash; (c) at minimum, grep the trunk log for CssSyntaxError and fail the step. (b) is the only one that also catches a stale dist from any other cause.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberately broken demo/input.css makes cargo xtask test-style and test-layout FAIL, not pass. The failure message names the stylesheet build, not a mount timeout or a ceiling breach. A negative control proves it: break input.css, watch the suite go red, restore, watch it go green.
notes: The trap that produced it is now documented in demo/input.css's own comment, but that only covers this one trigger. The general hole - a green audit run against a stylesheet that failed to build - is what this bead is for. Related: the same class of silent staleness bit an agent earlier the same day when a concurrent session's trunk build rewrote demo/dist under a running suite, causing 9 layout tests to fail on untouched pages.
close_reason: Fixed in c51010c. Design covers all THREE failure modes, not just tailwind's exit code: the stylesheet build moved out of trunk's swallowed pre_build hook into demo/build-css.mjs invoked by xtask (fails loud), plus a run-unique marker republished into dist and asserted by harness_at - so a stale dist from ANY cause is caught, which an exit-code-only fix would miss. Marker is an unmatchable id RULE rather than a comment, because comments are absent from the CSSOM and stripped by the release minifier. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN BOTH DIRECTIONS: with the original trap re-created, test-style and test-layout both went RED at exit 1 naming the stylesheet build, and the running-server path panicked with STYLESHEET BUILD FAILED; restoring input.css returned 7/7 and 9/9 green. Marker proven inert byte-for-byte: report_layout_backlog identical across all 7 swept pages, 214 lines of violations, same scanned/total per page, backlog 52 both times. Failure mode 2 confirmed twice - deliberately, and then by accident when an sccache failure left trunk serving a stale dist and all 7 style tests correctly reported the stylesheet instead of a bogus ceiling breach.

Not a regression in this repo - the engine got stricter under us (pixelproof-style-audit is a PATH dep, so two commits landed live with no commit here): 9856c40 models shadow COLOUR HUE and INSET in ShadowSpec, and 9b5020a skips inert layers and measures font resolution. title: [streaming] Add an authenticated fetch-based SSE hook with owned lifecycle
description: The framework use_event_source hook correctly owns native EventSource lifecycle, but EventSource cannot set Authorization headers. Applications that legitimately fall back from cookies to bearer sessions must either duplicate fetch/ReadableStream parsing and reconnection or lose live updates. 4iiz-Office issue op-rrp9 needs a universal client primitive; authentication policy and any short-lived ticket issuance remain application/server concerns.
acceptance_criteria: Add a direct Leptos hook for authenticated fetch-based server-sent-event streams that accepts caller-supplied safe headers without putting credentials in the URL; incrementally parses SSE framing across arbitrary chunk boundaries, including named events, data lines, ids, retry hints, comments, CRLF, and final partial buffers; owns AbortController, reader, callbacks, timers, and cleanup without leaks; exposes connected/reconnecting/stopped and parse/transport diagnostics; supports bounded backoff, Last-Event-ID, explicit stop, owner cleanup, and injectable sleep/fetch seams for deterministic native tests; provide typed JSON convenience matching use_event_source_json; document when to use native EventSource versus authenticated fetch streaming; include wasm/browser reconnect and unmount coverage; never log or expose authorization headers.
close_reason: use_event_source_fetch in utils: fetch+ReadableStream SSE with caller headers per (re)connect, pure SseParser (WHATWG grammar) + take_utf8_prefix, retry:/Last-Event-ID reconnection, abort-on-cleanup. Reuses EventSourceHandle. 14 unit tests.

title: [modal] Support specific accessible dialog names and descriptions
description: Modal hardcodes aria-label="Modal" on every native dialog and exposes no label, aria-labelledby, or aria-describedby contract. Consumer dialogs render visible translated headings inside ModalBox, but assistive technology hears only the same generic English word for every dialog. Raw dialogs also persist because callers cannot connect a title/description through the component API. Consumer finding: office-perf op-99t7/op-cy77.2.
acceptance_criteria: Add explicit mutually coherent accessible-name and description props supporting direct localized labels and labelledby/describedby IDs; remove the hardcoded generic name when a specific contract is supplied while retaining a safe backward-compatible fallback. Document title/description wiring, ensure open/close focus behavior and native dialog semantics remain intact, and add DOM/axe/browser tests for unique localized names, descriptions, missing/duplicate IDs, nested heading content and backward compatibility. Migrate office-perf dialogs once the path dependency includes the change.
close_reason: Modal gains label / labelled_by / described_by; labelled_by suppresses aria-label so the visible translated heading is what AT hears; generic fallback only when unnamed. Typo'd aria_modal attr removed. Commit b1b259c; browser test modal_is_named_by_its_visible_heading.

title: [field] Make labels, help text, and validation programmatically associated
description: Field documents itself as a form-field wrapper, but it renders the visible <label> and the children as siblings inside a div and supplies neither for/id nor aria-labelledby. Help, warning, success and error lines are also unrelated <label> elements without aria-describedby/aria-errormessage. A screen reader therefore cannot reliably associate any of this text with the Input/Select/Textarea child. Input itself has no first-class accessible-label/description props. Consumer finding: office-perf op-99t7/op-cy77.2.
acceptance_criteria: Define one direct accessible association contract across Field and the standard form controls. Prefer generated/stable IDs plus label for, aria-describedby and aria-invalid/aria-errormessage, or an equally semantic wrapper shape that works for every supported child; do not rely on placeholder text. Ensure multiple fields do not collide, optional caller IDs remain stable, error/help IDs update without dangling references, required state is announced, and existing visual markup/classes remain compatible. Add DOM/axe/browser tests covering Input, Select and Textarea in default/error/help/required states plus documentation and demo examples; provide a migration path for existing callers.
close_reason: Field mints ids + provides FieldContext; Input/Select/Textarea auto-consume it: label[for]->id, help via aria-describedby, error via aria-errormessage + aria-invalid (mirrored into describedby). Pure field_line shared by render and context. See git log (commit after b1b259c); browser test field_wires_label_help_and_error_to_the_input.

title: [day scheduler] Add accessible event activation and keyboard movement contracts

The office-perf Day Planner therefore reimplements scheduler blocks and HTML5 drag/drop in application code; its clickable/draggable divs have no keyboard-equivalent workflow. This is a universal interaction responsibility, not an app-local workaround. Consumer finding: office-perf op-03ix/op-99t7.

Provide a direct custom-content escape hatch only if needed for consumer parity without exposing layout internals. Keep pointer behavior and pure lane geometry intact, respect reduced motion/focus styling, and add unit, DOM, browser keyboard, demo and backwards-compatibility tests. title: SlaChip: fmt_duration lost d2d-ui's overflow clamp in the port, so a multi-year breach wrapped out of the pill
description:
FIXED 2026-07-31 (raised from 4iiz-Office op-jmxb).

THE DEFECT: against real data every breached row in the Office Performance Consultant Task Queue rendered its SLA chip as two lines -- "+1981d 13h" then "over" -- with the word "over" sitting on or below the pill's red border. Twelve of twelve visible rows. The breach magnitudes were genuine (+1981d, +1785d, +1462d ... from 2021-2023 due dates); the number was right and the chip could not hold it.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT THE FORMAT, IT IS THE COMMENT. sla_chip_fmt_duration said "Ported verbatim from d2d-ui's fmt_duration". It was not verbatim. d2d-ui carries a clamp this port dropped:
    if days > MAX_DISPLAY_DAYS { format!(">{MAX_DISPLAY_DAYS}d") }   // 99
added by 4iiz-Office op-4tr for exactly this failure. The desktop had already solved it; the web port arrived without the guard; and the "verbatim" claim is what kept the gap invisible, because anyone comparing the two would trust the comment rather than the code.

WHY NOT SIMPLY RE-ADD THE CLAMP: ">99d" is bounded, and it is bounded by DISCARDING ORDER -- 100 days overdue and 5.4 years overdue both render ">99d", so in a queue sorted by urgency the rows that most need distinguishing become identical at the very top of the list.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD -- precision that degrades with magnitude:
    >= 365d -> "5.4y"     >= 10d -> "364d"     > 0d -> "9d 5h"
    >= 10h  -> "23h"      > 0h   -> "9h 30m"   else -> "45m"
The finer unit is dropped exactly when the coarser one reaches two digits, because that is where it stops informing and starts costing the width that broke the pill. This BOUNDS the breached label at 12 chars ("+9d 23h over") for ANY input -- the same width the design already fits. The old form had no bound at all, so it was permanently one unusually stale record away from breaking again.
Also added whitespace-nowrap to the chip: the formatter bounds what is normally produced, the class makes "should never wrap" into "cannot wrap".

TESTS: 4 new, including every_label_fits_the_one_line_pill, which sweeps ~1 minute to 100 years in both directions and asserts the 12-char bound -- a property test, not an example. Full suite 1957 + doctests green, clippy -D warnings clean.
VERIFIED in a real browser against the live dev mirror: all 12 rows now read "+5.4y over" / "+4.9y over" / ... on one line inside the border. Screenshot in 4iiz-Office docs/ui-audit/op-jmxb-sla-chip-fixed.png.

FOLLOW-UP FILED in Rust-DeskApp: d2d-ui should adopt the same scheme so the two surfaces stop disagreeing about the same number.

title: Layout-audit sweep does not return through the Rust CDP binding
description:
Blocks ldui-dg2 from being wired into verify-full.

The sweep LOGIC is verified. Run verbatim through Chrome DevTools against the
live demo it completes in ~1.5s per page and produces correct results across all
six audited pages (button/alert/card/tab/data-table/kanban): 0 overlaps, and the
grid/internal counts that are now the committed ceilings in
tests/layout_audit_smoke.rs.

What does not work is shipping that same JS into the page from the Rust test:

  tests/common/mod.rs::layout_report -> h.page().evaluate*(SWEEP_JS)

Symptoms tried, in order:
  1. evaluate() with '(() => {...})()'  -> HANGS with no error, no panic, past
     the 60s wait_for_selector budgets, i.e. it is not the mount wait.
  2. evaluate() with 'JSON.stringify(function(){...}())' -> still hangs.
  3. evaluate_function() with 'function () {...}'   -> fast, clean error:
     -32000 'Given expression does not evaluate to a function'
  4. evaluate_function() with '(function () {...})' -> same -32000.

NOT an environment problem: the pre-existing reactivity_smoke suite passes 6/6
in 17.5s against the same server, same harness, same Chrome. It only ever
evaluates SHORT expressions (~50 bytes) via the same page().evaluate.

Leading hypothesis, untested: expression SIZE. SWEEP_JS is ~7KB; every call that
works elsewhere is tiny. Worth testing with a long-but-trivial expression (e.g. a
6KB '1+1+1+...') to separate size from shape before touching the sweep again.
Second hypothesis: chromiumoxide's Evaluation heuristic picking callFunctionOn
for a string starting with '(' and containing '=>'.

Until this is fixed:
- layout_step() exists and 'cargo xtask test-layout' is wired, but it is
  deliberately NOT added to verify-full -- a hanging step would hang the gate.
- The tests keep their #[ignore], so a bare 'cargo test' is unaffected.

Do not 'fix' this by loosening the assertions. The assertions are right; the
transport is not.
close_reason: block_on-inside-async deadlock in pixelproof-web's Harness::drop, fixed in PixelProof 126acfe. Drop went from infinite hang to 363us; layout suite passes 8/8. All three hypotheses on the ticket were wrong -- the sweep transported fine all along, the hang was in teardown.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
FIXED. Root cause was not in this repo, and not any of the three hypotheses
on this ticket.

The bug is a classic block_on-inside-async deadlock in the sibling PixelProof
crate:

  pixelproof-web/src/harness.rs  impl Drop for Harness
    let _ = futures::executor::block_on(self.browser.close());

browser.close() posts a message to the CDP handler task and awaits a oneshot
reply, so it can only resolve while that handler is being polled. Drop runs
inside the async test body, so block_on parks the very runtime thread the
handler needs. close() never completes; the drop deadlocks with Chrome pinned
at 100% CPU.

What made it hard: the failure is in TEARDOWN. Every assertion had already
passed; cargo just never got to print 'ok' because the test function could not
return. It is indistinguishable from a hung request unless you bracket the
phases. A probe that printed around each step settled it in one run:

  harness_at       1.71s   ok
  evaluate tiny    0.85ms  ok
  evaluate sweep   2.83ms  ok   <- the sweep was ALWAYS fine
  drop harness     hangs        <- the actual bug

All three hypotheses recorded here were wrong, and worth recording as wrong:
- Expression SIZE: disproved. A 6834-byte expression returned in 1.56ms.
- chromiumoxide's function-detection heuristic: not implicated.
- evaluate vs evaluate_function: a red herring I introduced myself while
  chasing the hang. evaluate() works; switching to evaluate_function() was
  what produced the -32000 'Given expression does not evaluate to a function',
  because CDP callFunctionOn rejects a parenthesised function expression.
  Reverted to evaluate().

Fix (PixelProof 126acfe): Drop no longer blocks — it aborts the handler task
and lets Browser's own Drop terminate the child, which is safe because
chromiumoxide spawns it with kill_on_drop. Added Harness::close() for callers
wanting the clean CDP handshake. Drop went from an infinite hang to 363us.

Likely also the cause of the stale ldui-pp-profile-* directories these suites
leave behind (93 of them at one point) -- the browser was never closing
cleanly.

Result: tests/layout_audit_smoke.rs now passes 8/8 in 26.6s, both directly and
through 'cargo xtask test-layout' with its own spawned server. layout_step()
is now wired into verify-full.

title: Migrate off daisyUI 4 form classes (form-control / label-text) — they are no-ops in daisyUI 5

title: Decide whether 2px is a sanctioned decorative sub-unit
description:
Blocks ldui-dg2. Surfaced by the ldui-lua audit (finding F3).

9 of the 14 off-4-grid occurrences in the web source are 2px, and every one is
a decorative accent rather than layout spacing:

  login_screen/component.rs:282      space-y-0.5
  metric_row/component.rs:38         gap-0.5
  result_list/component.rs:56,189,221  gap-0.5
  toolbar/component.rs:62,291        h-0.5, -bottom-0.5  (underline bar)
  vertical_steps/component.rs:56,59,119,133  w-0.5, mt-0.5  (connector rail)

title: Add automated spacing + overlap checks to the PixelProof web suite
description:
Workstream D, web half. Turn the article's manual '10-minute spacing audit' into a permanent test, reusing the reactivity-test seam that already exists (?pp-freeze=1 + window.__APP_DEBUG__ -- see the web-pixelproof-parity memory).

Three assertions over the rendered DOM, via getBoundingClientRect:
1. Overlap: no two visible sibling elements' boxes may intersect. This is the regression test for the entire class of bug where a component grows and its neighbour does not move.
2. Grid: every gap between vertically adjacent siblings, and every inset from a container to its first child, must be a member of the canonical scale. Report violations with selector and value.
3. Internal <= external: for every container, padding must be <= the gap to its siblings. This is the check that catches two cards visually merging.

The desktop half builds the same three checks over its SemanticNode tree via /api/dom; the rect data is equivalent, so the assertion logic should read the same on both faces. Land the detector BEFORE the token migration so the backlog is enumerated rather than guessed.
close_reason: Suite passes 8/8 via cargo xtask test-layout and is wired into verify-full. Zero overlaps and zero off-grid gaps we own; remaining counts are daisyUI's 6px internal gaps, held as committed ceilings.

title: Drive web line-height from the shared typography::LINE_* ramp
description:

The web side inherits the same tokens through the path dep. Do the equivalent:
- Emit the LINE_* ramp as CSS custom properties (--line-body etc.) alongside the existing spacing scale.
- Set an explicit line-height on every type-ramp class instead of inheriting the browser/Tailwind default, so a stack of N lines lands on the grid on both faces.
- Verify a paragraph of body text occupies exactly N * 20px, not N * (font metric).

title: Adopt the shared spacing & vertical-rhythm system in the web UI framework
description:
Port the spacing/sizing rules audited in Rust-DeskApp (docs/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-system-audit.md) to the Leptos/daisyUI face of the framework, so desktop and web share one system rather than two dialects.

SOURCE
- Article: Mohit Phogat, "The Spacing System That Makes Every UI Look More Intentional" (Medium, 2026-06-22).
- Desktop audit + plan: C:\dev\Rust-DeskApp\docs\plans\2026-07-26-spacing-system-audit.md

THE RULES WE ARE ADOPTING
1. One base unit. Every spacing value is a multiple of 8, with 4 as the sanctioned sub-unit. Canonical scale 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96.
2. Internal <= external. A container's padding must be <= the gap between it and its neighbours, or the containers visually merge.
3. Tokens, never raw values. No arbitrary px/rem in a margin, padding or gap.
4. Deterministic line height. One grid-aligned line-height per type-ramp step; no per-component guesses.
5. The audit is automated, not manual (see child issue on the DOM overlap/grid checks).

WHY THIS LANDS ON THE WEB SIDE TOO
leptos-daisyui-rs consumes ui-tokens from Rust-DeskApp via a path dep, so the token work done there (extended spacing scale, new line-height ramp, stroke family) arrives here for free -- but only if components actually reference the tokens instead of hardcoding Tailwind spacing utilities. The desktop audit found the tokens existed and were used in 5 of ~105 component files; the same question has to be asked here before assuming we are clean.

SCOPE
- Audit the 96 components for off-scale spacing and for Tailwind utilities used in place of tokens.
- Map ui_tokens::spacing + the new typography::LINE_* ramp onto CSS custom properties / a Tailwind theme extension, so one scale drives both faces.
- Enforce the internal-to-external rule where components nest (Card, Modal, Drawer, Table, Form control + label + helper text).
- Add the automated spacing/overlap checks to the existing PixelProof web suite (see web-pixelproof-parity memory: the ?pp-freeze=1 seam + window.__APP_DEBUG__ oracle already exist).

NOT IN SCOPE
- Adopting upstream's workspace restructure (Option B still holds: stay flat, cherry-pick).
- Changing the daisyUI theme palette. This is spacing and sizing only.

SEQUENCING
Mirror the desktop order: line-height determinism first, then the automated detector, then the token migration. Migrating tokens before the rhythm is pinned changes pixels without fixing anything and burns the visual baselines twice.
close_reason: All five rules satisfied and enforced; verify-full 12/12 including the layout audit and the real wasm build. Zero overlaps, zero off-grid gaps and zero internal>external violations that we own across the six audited pages. Three pre-existing bugs found and fixed along the way (daisyUI 4 form classes, the pixelproof-web drop deadlock, the CRLF drift check).

title: DataTable: sort comparator compares cells as strings, so money/number columns sort wrong ($1,000 < $900)
description:
Requested by 4iiz-inventory (bead bd_4iiz-inventory-3f5.5). Paired with the same defect in the d2d-ui sibling (Rust-DeskApp beads-gaf0) -- please keep the two designs aligned.

## The bug

DataTable's sort comparator compares cell values as STRINGS:

    // components/data_table/component.rs, sorted_indices memo
    let a_val = data_vec.get(a).and_then(|row| row.get(col_id)).map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
    let b_val = data_vec.get(b).and_then(|row| row.get(col_id)).map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
    match sort_order.get() {
        SortOrder::Asc  => a_val.cmp(b_val),
        SortOrder::Desc => b_val.cmp(a_val),
    }

So any column holding a formatted number sorts LEXICOGRAPHICALLY:

    "$1,000"  <  "$900"     because '1' < '9'
    "525"     <  "9"        days-in-stage
    "10%"     <  "9%"

Since Column::new() is SORTABLE BY DEFAULT (only Column::new_non_sortable opts out), any
consumer who puts money or durations in a table gets a wrong sort with no warning. That is
worse than no sort: the user believes they are looking at the largest balances and they are
not.

## What this component already gets RIGHT (please preserve it)

It sorts an INDEX PERMUTATION (`sorted_indices`) and never mutates `data`, so row identity
survives sorting by construction. The d2d-ui sibling mutates rows in place and corrupts its
own selection state as a result (Rust-DeskApp beads-e476). This design is the correct one --
the only thing wrong here is the comparator.

## Suggested fix

Give the column a sort TYPE, or the cell a typed key. Options:

  (a) add `sort_as: SortAs::{Text, Number, Date}` (default Text) to Column, and parse/compare
      accordingly -- Number strips currency symbols, thousands separators, %, and compares as
      f64 with a total order (handle NaN/absent deterministically);
  (b) allow a per-column comparator callback;
  (c) let a row supply a typed sort key per column alongside the display string.

(a) is the smallest change for consumers and matches how our columns are actually declared.

## Acceptance

- ["$900", "$1,000", "$85"] with sort_as: Number sorts ascending to ["$85", "$900", "$1,000"].
- ["9", "525", "10"] sorts ascending to ["9", "10", "525"].
- Text columns are unchanged and remain the default.
- Empty / absent cells sort consistently and are NOT conflated with zero -- an em dash means
  "not measured", which is a different thing from 0 and must not sort as 0.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Fixed. Design (option (a) from the report), so the d2d-ui sibling (beads-gaf0) can mirror it:

- New `SortAs { Text (default), Number, Date }` in `src/components/data_table/sort.rs`; `Column.sort_as` + builder `Column::with_sort_as(SortAs::Number)`. Text is the default, so every existing table is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `parse_number` strips currency symbols, thousands separators, %, and reads accounting parens as negative: "$1,000.50" -> 1000.5, "(1,234)" -> -1234, "9%" -> 9. `parse_date` takes ISO-8601 (date or datetime) and US M/D/YYYY, packing to a comparable YYYYMMDDhhmmss key.
- MISSING != ZERO: a blank / em-dash / unparseable cell is missing and sorts LAST in BOTH directions (spreadsheet behaviour), so a desc sort still opens on the largest real value instead of a wall of dashes. Comparison uses f64::total_cmp, so the comparator stays a valid total order.
- The index-permutation sort (the thing this component already got right) is untouched: only the comparator changed, so row identity / selected_rows still survive a sort by construction.

Acceptance verified in the browser (demo /components/data-table, new 'Typed Sorting' section), not just in unit tests:
- Balance asc: ($1,250.50) | $85 | $900 | $1,000  -- and desc reverses it.
- Days asc: 9, 10, 525, then the em dash; desc: 525, 10, 9, and the em dash STILL last.
- Opened (Date) sorts chronologically both ways.
23 unit tests in sort.rs cover the parsers, the missing-value rule and the acceptance cases.

title: .beads/issues.jsonl export is stale — closures live only in the local Dolt DB
description: The git-tracked .beads/issues.jsonl does not reflect the Dolt DB. It contains 23 issues, all status=closed, and does NOT contain ldui-b08 (closed 2026-07-10) or ldui-e8o (created 2026-07-10). So the JSONL export -- the git-backed recovery path -- has stopped keeping up with bd writes. Risk: if the local Dolt DB in .beads/dolt/ldui is lost, recent issue state is unrecoverable from git. 'bd dolt push' to the fork now works (see ldui-e8o), which mitigates but does not fix this: the JSONL is what a fresh clone reads. Investigate auto-flush (config: no-auto-flush, flush-debounce) and whether the pre-commit hook that used to run 'bd sync --flush-only' was disabled by the bd v1.0 upgrade that removed the 'bd sync' subcommand (see kv.memory.bd-v1-pre-commit-hook-fix -- that memory notes this repo's .git/hooks/pre-commit still has the bug and was never patched).
acceptance_criteria: A fresh 'bd export' (or the commit hook) writes ldui-b08 and ldui-e8o into .beads/issues.jsonl, and the file is committed. Subsequent bd close operations update the JSONL without manual intervention.
notes: DIAGNOSED, not fixed. 'bd export' itself works: a probe export to a temp file yields 77 issues (2 open, 75 closed) and DOES contain ldui-b08, ldui-e8o and ldui-izn. The tracked .beads/issues.jsonl has only 23 (all closed). So the export code path is healthy; what is broken is the auto-flush that should refresh the tracked file after mutations. Ruled out: the stale 'bd sync --flush-only' pre-commit hook theory -- core.hooksPath=.githooks, and no hook under .githooks/, .git/hooks/ or .beads/hooks/ references 'bd sync'. Deliberately NOT auto-fixed: overwriting issues.jsonl (23 -> 77 entries) at session end could disturb beads' import path, and off-machine durability is already restored now that 'bd dolt push' to the fork works (ldui-e8o). Next step: work out why auto-flush is not firing (config keys no-auto-flush / flush-debounce, and note .beads/beads.left.jsonl + export-state.json exist, suggesting a compaction/split scheme that may explain the 23-issue subset). Then run 'bd export --output .beads/issues.jsonl' and commit.
close_reason: Root cause was NOT a broken auto-flush. The .githooks/pre-commit hook intentionally early-exits for the Dolt backend (grep '"backend":"dolt"' -> exit 0), because the Dolt backend syncs via 'bd dolt push/pull', not JSONL. The repo migrated to Dolt on 2026-05-28 (last issues.jsonl commit f2caf01), so the tracked JSONL froze at a 23-issue snapshot by design while the DB grew to 77. The 'closures live only in local DB' risk was real only until the Dolt remote was repointed to the fork (ldui-e8o) -- 'bd dolt push' now backs everything up off-machine. Resolution: refreshed .beads/issues.jsonl to the current 77-issue state via 'bd export' and committed it (665acd4) as a human-readable/PR-visible snapshot. Going forward it's a manual convenience mirror ('bd export --output .beads/issues.jsonl' when git should reflect current state); the authoritative backup is 'bd dolt push'. Verified DB intact after export (open beads unchanged).

title: markdown ThemeContext signals disposed while global observer holds them (AiChat WASM panic)
description: Browser smoke (ldui-0wf) found: sending any message in the AiChat demo panics the whole WASM app: 'At src/markdown/theme.rs:46:34 you tried to access a reactive value defined at theme.rs:100:18 but it has already been disposed', followed by RuntimeError: unreachable and a follow-on 'RefCell already borrowed' panic. Root cause: use_theme() creates RwSignals owned by the first calling component's reactive owner (theme.rs:100-101) and registers them with install_theme_observer (global, once per document). AiChat rebuilds MessageBubble/MarkdownView on every poll tick, so the first bubble's owner is disposed while the global observer + subsequent palette() calls (theme.rs:46) still reference the dead signals. Fix: give ThemeContext signals document lifetime (create under a detached/leaked root owner or thread_local singleton), independent of any component scope.
close_reason: Both fixed in 05260cd and verified live in the browser smoke session. ldui-i4t: ThemeContext is now a thread_local document-lifetime singleton whose signals are created under a deliberately parentless leaked Owner (document_root_owner via Owner unset/new/set), so the global MutationObserver can't outlive them — AiChat send no longer panics; reviewer verified the ownership trick against reactive_graph 0.2.14 source; regression test added in 44d7c52. ldui-4i0: performance.memory now read as a property via js_sys::Reflect::get (Performance web-sys feature added) — no more per-tick TypeError. title: Add semantic numeric presentation to EntityColumn
description: The Office Contribution, Conversations Report, Finances, and NPS Surveys conversions repeatedly use render_with only to wrap canonical numeric, currency, percentage, and duration text in right-aligned tabular-number spans. Typed sorting is tracked separately by ldui-96t; this opportunity concerns presentation. Repeating page-local renderers obscures the common intent, creates inconsistent header and compact alignment, and makes simple numeric columns look like custom rich content.
design: Add framework-owned column presentation metadata for horizontal alignment and tabular numerals, exposed through small typed builders such as align_end and tabular_numbers. Keep number, currency, percentage, and duration formatting caller-owned through the canonical text callback. Define precedence with render_with instead of introducing domain formatters.
acceptance_criteria: A text column can opt into start, center, or end alignment and tabular numerals without render_with. Wide headers and cells align coherently through resize, reorder, hide, sort, and horizontal scroll. Default compact rendering has an intentional documented label/value alignment. Canonical full text remains the accessibility and export value. Rich renderers remain source-compatible with a documented precedence rule. Forced-colors and responsive browser fixtures cover signed, optional, currency-like, percentage-like, and long numeric text.

title: Separate EntityTable column-chooser trigger presentation from its accessible label
description: EntityTable currently uses EntityTableTexts.choose_columns as both the visible dropdown trigger and its aria-label. Office requires the compact gear-style chooser next to table quick actions. A consumer can either show the full localized phrase or replace it with a glyph, but using a glyph also replaces the accessible name. The trigger therefore lacks a safe icon-only or custom presentation seam.
design: Keep the localized accessible name in EntityTableTexts and give the chooser a framework-owned icon treatment or an optional presentation-only trigger slot. The table continues to own placement, disclosure semantics, focus restoration, and the chooser menu; consumers must not replace those behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: The default remains source-compatible and has a meaningful localized accessible name. A compact icon-style trigger can be selected without changing that name. The dropdown remains end-aligned and visible at the right viewport edge, including beside caller toolbar actions. Keyboard activation, Escape dismissal, focus restoration, forced-colors presentation, and compact widths are covered in the browser fixture. Supplying custom presentation cannot remove the button role or accessible name.

title: Add typed sort-key helpers to EntityColumn
description: EntityColumn text columns sort by normalized strings unless every consumer writes a two-row comparator with sortable_by. Operational satellite conversions repeatedly sort integer counts, minute totals, dates, and optional values. The current API is correct but boilerplate-heavy, and accidentally relying on the text fallback produces lexical order such as 10 before 2. A typed key API would make the common correct path concise and auditable.
design: Add one or more typed sort-key builders for common ordered values while retaining sortable_by for domain-specific comparators. Prefer an implementation that extracts or normalizes a key once per row when practical, preserves stable system-order tie breaking, and makes null ordering explicit rather than inferred from display text.
acceptance_criteria: Consumers can declare numeric, date/time, string, and optional-value ordering without writing a left/right comparator. Numeric ordering proves 2 precedes 10; signed and optional values follow documented policies; descending and ordered multi-sort remain correct; equal keys preserve stable system order. Existing text sorting and sortable_by remain source-compatible. Unit tests cover each key family and a browser fixture proves visible order and sort metadata.

title: Add reusable text-overflow policies to EntityColumn
description: DataTable supports text truncation, but EntityTable has no typed overflow policy. Office No-Hires had to replace an otherwise plain Why this rank cell with a custom rich renderer solely to clip it to two lines, and the next satellite conversions have the same long narrative fields. Repeating page-local Tailwind renderers makes clipping inconsistent and can separate displayed text from the column text used for accessibility, sorting, compact rendering, and export.
design: Add presentation metadata to EntityColumn for ordinary wrapping, single-line ellipsis, and bounded multi-line clipping. Preserve the existing text callback as the canonical full value. The framework should apply the policy consistently in wide and default compact rendering and expose the full value accessibly, without changing sort or preference identity.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can opt a text column into single-line ellipsis or a positive line-clamp count without supplying render_with. The wide cell honors the declared width and never expands the row past the policy. Default compact rows apply an intentional documented policy. The canonical full text remains available to assistive technology and generic export without duplicate spoken content. Rich renderers remain source-compatible and have an explicit precedence rule. Focused render and browser cases cover one-line, two-line, long unbroken content, resized columns, and compact layout.

title: Expose a dedicated navigation-row layout in PageHeader
description: PageHeader always composes its back slot in the same title cluster on desktop and only stacks it on compact screens. The approved Office No-Hires layout requires Back on its own row above the page heading at every width, so the satellite bypasses the opinionated back slot with a page-local wrapper. Add an explicit layout choice or navigation slot that preserves semantic heading order without consumer CSS or duplicate markup.

title: Gantt dependency-preview line uses dead daisyUI 4 vars in a stroke= attribute — likely invisible today
description: src/components/gantt/timeline/dependency_preview.rs:50,52 hardcode 'var(--fallback-su,oklch(var(--su)/1))' and the --wa equivalent, emitted at :62 as stroke=move || stroke_color.get(). With no valid resolution the whole oklch() is invalid, the presentation attribute is dropped, and stroke falls back to its initial value NONE - so the dependency-drag preview line is almost certainly not rendering at all today. (2) Independently, this is a var() inside a stroke= PRESENTATION ATTRIBUTE, the exact hazard src/charts/paint.rs exists to eliminate: SVG2 parses presentation attributes with the property's isolated value grammar, so custom-property substitution is not specified to run there, and the SVG WG has an open request (Nov 2025) to specify or forbid it. src/components/gantt/timeline/timeline_markers.rs:460,474 have the same shape with a CALLER-SUPPLIED colour, so a consumer passing var(--color-primary) lands it straight in stroke=/fill=.

Then route through crate::charts::paint - but note attrs_for (src/charts/paint.rs:45) returns the WHOLE style value and dependency_preview.rs:67 already carries a static style='opacity: 0.7; pointer-events: none;', so this needs a style-MERGING variant of attrs_for, not a second call site. comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Task 12 break-and-revert executed against office-perf-web, 2026-08-09, at 1440x900
against one fixed bundle (build 03:19). Baseline and final runs both: 4 passed, exit 0,
zero slack notes. All artifacts restored byte-identical (md5 + the font's sha384 back to
`.bundle-ready`'s manifest value).

METHOD. Not `input.css`. That repo has a live concurrent session committing every few
minutes, so the break window was moved off any tracked file: the controls edit the BUILT
stylesheet in `crates/office-perf-web/dist/` (gitignored) and the suite is driven by the
already-compiled `style_audit` test binary. The direct driver was first proven equivalent
to `cargo make test-style` by reproducing the green baseline exactly.

Two traps found while getting this right, both of which silently fake a "detection":
- **Subresource Integrity.** Trunk emits `<link ... integrity="sha384-...">`, so ANY edit
  to `output-*.css` makes the browser DISCARD THE WHOLE STYLESHEET. The first attempt
  rendered the app unstyled, `--font-sans` was undefined, `body_font_family` read back
  "Times New Roman", and the suite "failed" with typography 41-57 on every route. That is
  not the audit detecting a font regression; it is the audit comparing against garbage.
  The sha384 must be recomputed and index.html rewritten with every edit.
- **`.shadow-card` cannot be the depth target.** Confirmed PixelProof-gbg from the DOM:
  a card computes as five layers, four inert
  (`rgba(0,0,0,0) 0px 0px 0px 0px` x4, then `rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0px 1px 15px 0px`), so it
  already reports 1 violation whatever `--shadow-card` holds. One violation per element,
  then break -> corrupting `--shadow-card` moves NO count. The depth control therefore
  targets `.btn:not(.btn-ghost):not(.btn-link)`, which `office_profile` declares and which
  is clean at baseline.

=============================================================================
CONTROL 1 (typography) - THE BRIEF'S LITERAL STEP 1 DOES NOT FAIL. NEW FINDING.
=============================================================================

Commenting out the Manrope `@font-face` block leaves the suite GREEN:

    test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; ... finished in 10.70s   REALEXIT=0

Mechanism, probed in-page with the block removed:

    document.fonts.check('16px "Manrope"') -> true
    document.fonts.size                    -> 0        (FontFaceSet EMPTY)
    getComputedStyle(body).fontFamily      -> "Manrope, -apple-system, ... sans-serif"
    getComputedStyle(body).fontWeight      -> "500"

Both font rules in the engine sweep are blind to this. Rule 1
(`!document.fonts.check(...)`) is vacuously TRUE because no face matches, so nothing is
"unloaded". Rule 2 (per-element first-family string) never fires because `--font-sans`
still NAMES Manrope, so every computed value still reads "Manrope" while the text
actually paints in the fallback. Nothing in the rendered computed style distinguishes
this from a healthy page.

So this regression is caught only STATICALLY, by `font_pipeline.rs`'s
`INPUT_CSS.contains(r#"font-family: "Manrope""#)` - the opposite of the brief's premise.

CONTROL 1b (typography, the regression that IS caught): keep the `@font-face` and make
the woff2 404 (the realistic "font pipeline broke" case - a face declared but unloadable).

    document.fonts.check('16px "Manrope"') -> false
    document.fonts.size                    -> 1, faces: [{family:"Manrope", status:"error"}]
    getComputedStyle(body).fontFamily      -> "Manrope, -apple-system, ..."   (IDENTICAL)

Note the computed family is byte-identical in both scenarios; rule 1 is the ONLY thing
separating them. Suite result - all four routes fail, +1 typography each, nothing else
moved:

    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 4 failed; ... finished in 10.27s   REALEXIT=101

    thread 'queue_style_is_within_ceiling' panicked at
      crates\office-perf-web\tests\style_audit.rs:383:85:
    /queue: over ceiling - typography: 5 > ceiling 4
    style audit for /queue: 210 scanned, 48 total across 7 families
      TYPOGRAPHY      0.00  @font-face  declared family "Manrope" is not loaded - text is
                                        silently falling back
      TYPOGRAPHY     10.00  nav.flex.flex-col > div.flex-1.min-h-0 > div.w-full.pt-1 ...
      TYPOGRAPHY     10.00  nav.flex.flex-col > div.flex-1.min-h-0 > div.w-full.pt-1 ...
      TYPOGRAPHY     10.00  nav.flex.flex-col > div.flex-1.min-h-0 > div.w-full.pt-1 ...
      TYPOGRAPHY     24.00  div.flex.items-start > div > div.flex.items-center > h2...

    /account:   typography: 6 > ceiling 5   (123 scanned, 39 total)
    /settings:  typography: 5 > ceiling 4   (116 scanned, 35 total)
    /dashboard: typography: 5 > ceiling 4   (119 scanned, 35 total)

The single added row is the `@font-face` selector on every route. Restored -> green.

=============================================================================
CONTROL 2 (depth) - FIRES AS CLAIMED
=============================================================================

`.btn:not(.btn-ghost):not(.btn-link)`'s two-layer resting lift replaced with the brief's
value, `0 9px 9px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5)`:

    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 4 failed; ... finished in 10.29s   REALEXIT=101

    DEPTH before -> after:  /queue 6->14   /account 2->6   /settings 1->8   /dashboard 1->13
    (no other family moved on any route)

    thread 'queue_style_is_within_ceiling' panicked at
      crates\office-perf-web\tests\style_audit.rs:383:85:
    /queue: over ceiling - depth: 14 > ceiling 6
    style audit for /queue: 210 scanned, 55 total across 7 families
      DEPTH      9.00  div.flex-1.overflow-y-auto > nav.navbar.border-b >
                       div.navbar-center.gap-2 > button.btn.ld-eased
                       box-shadow "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5) 0px 9px 9px 0px" not in the
                       declared shadow set
      DEPTH      9.00  nav.navbar.border-b > div.navbar-end.gap-3 >
                       div.join.join-horizontal > button.btn.ld-eased   (same detail)
      DEPTH      9.00  div.flex.flex-1 > div.flex-1.overflow-y-auto > div.alert.alert-error
                       > button.btn.ld-eased                            (same detail)
      DEPTH      9.00  div.card.ld-eased > div.card-body.p-4 > div.alert.alert-error >
                       button.btn.ld-eased                              (same detail)
      -- pre-existing, unchanged by the control:
      DEPTH      0.00  ... > button.relative.flex
                       box-shadow "rgb(0, 163, 215) 3px 0px 0px 0px inset" ...
      DEPTH      0.00  ... > div.card.bg-base-100
                       box-shadow "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 0px 0px 0px 0px, [x4], rgba(0, 0, 0,
                       0.05) 0px 1px 15px 0px" ...                      (PixelProof-gbg)
      DEPTH      0.00  ... > button.btn.ld-eased
                       box-shadow "oklch(0 0 0 / 0) 0px 0px 0px 0px inset, oklch(0 0 0 / 0)
                       0px 0px 0px 0px" ...

Restored -> green.

=============================================================================
WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE
=============================================================================

PROVES: the DEPTH ratchet detects a wrong elevation on a declared, currently-clean
component and fails the gate; the TYPOGRAPHY ratchet detects a declared font that fails
to LOAD; both recover exactly to baseline on restore; the ceilings have now been seen
failing rather than merely passing.

DOES NOT PROVE: that any part of the suite detects a *deleted* `@font-face` - measured,
it does not. It also does not prove anything about elements the sweep already reports:
one violation per element then break means a component that is ALREADY violating cannot
report "more", which is why a card was unusable as the depth target.
