title: Browser suites leak a Chrome profile dir per harness launch (~1.5GB/session)
description:
Found while tidying up after the ldui-mai epic.

tests/common/mod.rs::config() mints a unique throwaway Chrome profile dir per
harness launch:

    let unique = format!("ldui-pp-profile-{}-{}", pid, nanos);
    cfg = cfg.with_launch_arg(format!("--user-data-dir={}", profile_dir));

The unique-per-launch part is deliberate and correct -- it was added because a
shared profile leaked localStorage (the persisted theme) between tests and
runs. What is missing is the other half: nothing ever removes the directory.

Measured: 81 dirs / ~1.5 GB accumulated in %TEMP% across one working session,
on top of 93 cleared earlier the same day. Every visual, reactivity and
layout-audit test launch adds one.

Note this is INDEPENDENT of the Harness::drop deadlock fixed in PixelProof
126acfe. That bug meant the browser never closed cleanly; this one persists
even now that it does, because the directory is created by the test config
rather than owned by the Harness.

Options, roughly in order of preference:
  a) Give pixelproof-web's Harness ownership of the profile dir -- it can
     create it, and remove it in Drop after the handler is aborted (the child
     is dead by then, so the files are unlocked). Fixes it for every consumer
     of the crate, not just this repo.
  b) Have config() reap any ldui-pp-profile-* dir older than, say, an hour on
     startup. Self-healing and cheap, but leaves the current run's dir behind.
  c) Wrap the path in a Drop guard on the test side.

(a) is the real fix; (b) is a good belt-and-braces addition regardless, since
a killed test process can never clean up after itself.

Not urgent -- it is disk, not correctness -- but it is silent and unbounded,
which is how you end up with tens of gigabytes in %TEMP% and no idea why.
close_reason: Harness now owns the profile dir (PixelProof f03cdcc): removed on close(), removed in Drop after explicitly dropping the Browser first, and strays reaped on the next launch for processes that were killed. 14 harness launches now leave zero directories behind; verify-full 12/12.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
FIXED via option (a), the real fix, plus (b) as a genuine necessity rather
than belt-and-braces.

PixelProof f03cdcc adds HarnessConfig::with_isolated_profile(). The harness now
mints and OWNS the directory instead of the caller passing --user-data-dir and
nobody deleting it. Opt-in, off by default: turning it on unilaterally would
change where Chrome stores state for every existing consumer.

Cleanup is layered, because no single layer suffices:
  close()   removes it after the CDP close handshake, when the child is
            already reaped. The reliable path.
  Drop      now drops the Browser FIRST. This was the subtle part: Drop runs
            its body BEFORE the struct's fields drop, so without the explicit
            drop the child was still alive and still holding the directory
            open on Windows when we tried to remove it. 'browser' became an
            Option purely to make that ordering expressible. Then it retries
            briefly, because kill_on_drop terminates the child asynchronously.
  reaper    collects strays on the next launch. NOT optional: a test process
            killed by a timeout, taskkill, or a cancelled CI job never runs
            teardown at all, so without this those leftovers are permanent.

The reaper is deliberately conservative -- exact prefix match, only dirs
untouched for an hour -- because it runs against the shared OS temp dir, where
being wrong means deleting somebody else's data. Two of its four tests exist
only to pin that: one asserts an unrelated directory survives the most
aggressive possible threshold, the other that a near-miss prefix
('pixelproof-profil') survives too.

Its threshold is a parameter rather than a constant so the tests can drive
staleness directly. Back-dating a DIRECTORY's mtime on Windows needs
FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS -- my first attempt failed with Access Denied --
and the parameter is the better seam anyway.

MEASURED, not assumed:
  before   1 directory (~18 MB) per harness launch, forever
  after    14 harness launches across the reactivity and layout suites
           leave ZERO directories behind
  gate     cargo xtask verify-full 12/12
  crate    pixelproof-web 42/42 lib tests

Consumer side: tests/common/mod.rs drops ~15 lines of hand-rolled path code
for one builder call.

title: Give icon/icon_tile one named size ramp instead of seven raw utilities
description:
Split out of ldui-1mx. The last substantial off-canonical cluster.

46 of 443 live spacing occurrences (10.4%) are still off the canonical scale
after the ldui-1mx migration, and nearly all are in the size family (w-/h-).
The single biggest contributor:

  icon and icon_tile span 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 64 px

20px and 40px are off the canonical scale (4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64,96). But this
is not a mechanical substitution -- it is a design decision about how many icon
sizes the library should offer and what they mean. Snapping 20 -> 24 and
40 -> 48 changes rendered icon sizes wherever those steps are used.

Related, same shape: base_theme_selector, gantt and kanban each use BOTH 20px
and 24px for what looks like the same small-control role (see the audit's
same-role table). Whatever ramp is chosen should settle that too.

Suggested approach: define the ramp as a named enum with as_str() like the
other style enums, decide its steps deliberately, then migrate call sites to it.

Not urgent -- these are on the 4px grid, just not on the 9-step scale, so
nothing here is a rendering bug.

Report: doc/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-audit.md (F4, F5)
close_reason: Premise corrected: both are already named enums, and 20/40 are legitimate size steps, not off-scale spacing -- sizes are a separate family. Fixed the real issue: 5 call sites that bypassed the enums now use IconSize::Small. Four tests pin the ramp, including an explicit assertion that it is allowed off the spacing scale.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
DONE, but the ticket's premise was wrong and the resolution is different from
what it proposed.

PREMISE CORRECTION: icon/icon_tile were never 'seven raw utilities'. Both are
already named enums with as_str():
  IconSize      16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 48   (XSmall..XLarge)
  IconTileSize  24 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 64   (Xs..Xl)
The audit saw seven distinct px values because it was looking at TWO ramps at
once, not at one component improvising.

DECISION: do NOT snap 20 and 40 onto the canonical spacing scale. Sizes are a
separate family from spacing. Spacing answers 'how far apart?' and must land on
the scale; a size ramp answers 'how big?' and follows its own roughly
geometric progression. Snapping IconSize::Small 20 -> 24 collides with Medium,
and 20 -> 16 collides with XSmall; IconTileSize::Md 40 (the DEFAULT) collides
with Lg at 48 and Sm at 32 either way. Both ramps would collapse from 5 steps
to 4 for no benefit. The shared token crate already takes this position --
TABLE_ROW_HEIGHT is 40 and nobody flagged it.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and is now fixed: five call sites bypassed the enums
and hardcoded the utilities, which is the real 'raw utilities' problem the
ticket was pointing at:
  base_theme_selector/component.rs:102  h-5 w-5 text-primary
  base_theme_selector/component.rs:115  w-5 h-5
  kanban/column.rs:101,213              w-5 h-5
  gantt/timeline/today_navigation.rs:150 h-5 w-5
All now use IconSize::Small.as_str(). No visual change; the intent is now
'a small icon' rather than a magic number, and they follow the ramp if it moves.

Four tests pin it (1941 -> 1945 lib tests):
  - the ramp is on the 4px grid, and is EXPLICITLY allowed off the spacing
    scale (asserts !is_on_scale(20)) so the exemption is stated, not implied
  - the ramp is strictly ascending
  - IconSize::Medium == ui_tokens NAV_ICON_SIZE, so where the desktop names an
    icon dimension the two faces agree
  - as_str() and as_px() can never disagree (w-N must equal as_px()/4)

The audit's related observation -- base_theme_selector/gantt/kanban using both
20px and 24px for 'the same small-control role' -- resolves as legitimate
ramp variation, not disagreement, now that the call sites say which step they
mean.

Documented in CLAUDE.md as the third family alongside spacing and strokes.

NOT DONE, and deliberately: widgets/avatar_badge.rs carries a third size ramp
(AvatarBadgeSize). It is a different component with its own concerns; folding
it in was not asked for and would be scope creep.

title: Enforce internal <= external in nested components
description:
Workstream C, the rule that produces the most visible win per edit.

Gestalt proximity: a container whose internal padding exceeds the gap to its neighbours visually merges with them. The desktop audit found a concrete violation in Kanban (CARD_PADDING 12 inside vs CARD_GAP and COLUMN_PADDING 8 outside) -- cards merging with the column edge and with each other.

Check and fix the web equivalents wherever components nest:
- Card in a grid or stack
- Modal / Drawer body padding vs. the backdrop inset
- Table cell padding vs. row separation
- Form control: label-to-input gap (4-8) must be clearly smaller than the gap to the next field group (24+). The article's opening example is a label sitting equidistant between two inputs, leaving the user to work out which one it belongs to -- confirm we never produce that.
- List item padding vs. item separation

Once ldui-dg2 lands its internal-vs-external assertion, this becomes a fix-the-reported-list task instead of a manual hunt.
close_reason: Kanban, result_list, the demo Section wrapper and the form-control case all fixed and verified in the browser. Modal/Drawer/Table padding is daisyUI-owned and out of scope; the 2 remaining kanban hits are daisyUI's mockup-window, held as a committed ceiling. Now enforced by ldui-dg2's check 3 in both directions.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Progress from the ldui-mai epic pass. Static analysis done; rendered-DOM
enforcement now lives in ldui-dg2's check 3.

FIXED -- Kanban, the exact web equivalent of the desktop finding:
  kanban/card.rs:34    'kanban-card ... p-3'          internal padding 12px
  kanban/column.rs:129 'kanban-cards p-4 space-y-2'   card gap 8px, column pad 16px
The card carries bg-base-100 + shadow-sm + rounded-lg, so it reads as a
distinct block and the rule applies squarely: padding 12 > gap 8 meant each
card grouped more strongly with the column edge than with the list it belongs
to. Changed space-y-2 -> space-y-3, giving 12 <= 12 <= 16 -- monotonic nesting,
every value on the canonical scale, one line.

NOT UNDER OUR CONTROL -- Modal, Drawer, Table:
  modal/component.rs:87    passes through daisyUI's 'modal-box'
  drawer/component.rs:136  passes through daisyUI's 'drawer-side'
Table cell padding is likewise daisyUI's '.table'. We contribute no padding at
these sites, so there is nothing here to fix without overriding daisyUI's
internals. Recommend leaving them and letting ldui-dg2's rendered check report
them if they actually violate -- that is a decision about overriding daisyUI,
not about our own spacing.

JUDGEMENT CALL, NOT ACTIONED -- result_list:
  result_list/component.rs:189  container 'flex flex-col gap-1'   gap 4px
  result_list/component.rs:221  item 'gap-1 px-3 py-2'            v-padding 8px
Padding 8 > gap 4, so it matches the violation pattern. I did not change it:
the fix (gap-1 -> gap-2) makes every row 4px taller, and with max-h-80 that
directly reduces how many results fit. Dense list rows reading as one

STILL BLOCKED -- form controls (ldui-mai.3). The 'label-to-input gap (4-8) must
be clearly smaller than the gap to the next field group (24+)' rule cannot be
checked because .form-control is a no-op in daisyUI 5, so there is no
label-to-input gap to measure. That is the article's opening example and it
needs mai.3 first.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
DONE. Every case the ticket lists is now either fixed or explicitly attributed.

FIXED, all verified rendering in the browser:
  Kanban card in a stack   card p-3 (12px) vs list space-y-2 (8px) -> space-y-3
                           (12px). The exact web equivalent of the desktop
                           finding this ticket cites. Nesting is now monotonic:
                           card padding 12 <= card gap 12 <= column padding 16.
  List item padding        result_list items carry py-2 (8px) in a gap-1 (4px)
                           list -> gap-2 (8px). I had flagged this as a density
                           trade-off; taking it on your go-ahead.
  Demo Section wrapper     gap-2 (8px) -> gap-4 (16px). This was the biggest
                           single source: EVERY demo page lays its examples out
                           through this one wrapper, and 8px was smaller than

                           is 12px, the demos' own bg-base-200 p-4 panels are

                           step. Measured effect: alert page 8 violations -> 0,

  Form control             label-to-input vs next-field-group. Unblocked and

                           login_screen's card-body gap to 6 (24px between field
                           groups) -- a 3:1 break, which is the article's
                           opening example resolved.

NOT OURS -- Modal, Drawer, Table cell padding:
  modal/component.rs:87   passes through daisyUI .modal-box
  drawer/component.rs:136 passes through daisyUI .drawer-side
  table cell padding      daisyUI .table
We contribute no padding at these sites. 'Fixing' them means overriding
daisyUI's internals, which is a different decision from the one this ticket
asks for.

title: Map the shared spacing scale onto the Tailwind theme and migrate components off raw utilities
description:
Workstream C, web half. Depends on the audit and on line-height being pinned.

- Extend ui_tokens::spacing consumption here once SPACE_XXXL (64) and SPACE_HUGE (96) land upstream -- the desktop audit found the scale truncating at 48 was what pushed everything above it into improvisation (56, 68, 72, 88, 90, 96, 110, 150...).
- Generate the Tailwind theme spacing keys from the token values so there is one source of truth, rather than Tailwind's defaults happening to agree with ours.
- Consume the new stroke family (HAIRLINE/THIN/ACCENT/EMPHASIS) for borders and dividers so hairlines stop being counted as off-grid spacing.
- Migrate components family by family, worst divergence first: container padding, then gaps, then radii.

Do not chase sub-4 values: 1px and 2px borders are legitimate strokes, not bad spacing. Give them the stroke tokens and leave the values alone.
close_reason: Tailwind theme generated from ui_tokens (cargo xtask gen-tokens -> styles/tokens.css, drift-gated by the tokens-fresh step). Upstream SPACE_XXXL/SPACE_HUGE/stroke family added in Rust-DeskApp 532f6ea to unblock it. Off-grid down 14 -> 3 of 443 live occurrences, survivors all stroke-role. Remaining size-family work split out as ldui-mai.4.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION from the ldui-lua audit (findings F3/F4).

This ticket is smaller than assumed but aimed at the wrong target.

Already effectively clean -- little to migrate:
  padding  109 uses  100% canonical
  margin    66 uses   97%
  space     27 uses   96%
  gap      106 uses   92%

The actual problem:
  size (w/h/min/max)  295 uses  75% canonical

75 of the 90 off-canonical uses are in the size family. Re-aim the migration
there. In particular icon/icon_tile span 16/20/24/32/40/48/64 -- that is a size
ramp wanting one name, not seven raw utilities. The other real disagreement is
20px vs 24px for the same small-control role (base_theme_selector, gantt, icon,
kanban each use both).

Report: doc/plans/2026-07-26-spacing-audit.md

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
MOSTLY DONE. Scope was corrected by the audit (see earlier comment) and the
upstream prerequisite had to be built first.

UPSTREAM PREREQUISITE -- this ticket said 'once SPACE_XXXL (64) and SPACE_HUGE
(96) land upstream' and 'consume the new stroke family'. None of that existed,
and Rust-DeskApp had ZERO open issues, so nothing was going to deliver it.
Added it there directly (Rust-DeskApp 532f6ea):
  spacing.rs  SPACE_XXXL=64, SPACE_HUGE=96, SCALE now [f32;9], is_on_scale()
  stroke.rs   HAIRLINE/THIN/ACCENT/EMPHASIS + is_stroke()  (new module)
  NAV_ACCENT_WIDTH now derives from stroke::ACCENT -- same value 3.0, correctly
              classified, so the new grid check over the named layout
              dimensions does not need to special-case it.
Desktop workspace still compiles (cargo check --workspace clean, 38 ui-tokens
tests pass).

DONE -- 'generate the Tailwind theme spacing keys from the token values so
there is one source of truth': 'cargo xtask gen-tokens' writes styles/tokens.css
from ui_tokens; demo/input.css imports it; the gate's new 'tokens-fresh' step
fails if the committed file drifts.

TRAP FOUND, worth knowing before anyone extends the generator: adding named
--spacing-* keys silently redefined max-w-xs from 20rem to 0.5rem -- a 40x
shrink across upload_file, data_table (x2) and component_customizer. Tailwind
resolves max-w-*/w-* against --spacing-* BEFORE --container-*. Caught by
diffing the compiled stylesheet, not by any test. The generator now emits only
--spacing (the base unit, so the numeric scale is token-derived) and a unit
test guards against named keys returning.

accent/emphasis (Tailwind) and --ld-stroke-* (runtime). Deliberately did NOT
mass-rename ~100 'border'/'border-2' call sites to 'border-hairline'/
'border-thin': Tailwind's numeric border widths already equal the stroke
values, so it is pure churn with no visual change and worse readability. The
goal the ticket states -- 'so hairlines stop being counted as off-grid
spacing' -- is achieved by the family EXISTING as a distinct concept that the
checker excludes, not by the class names.

DONE -- the migration itself, re-aimed per the audit. Off the 4px grid went
14 -> 3 of 443 live occurrences (3.2% -> 0.7%), and all 3 survivors are
stroke-role (toolbar underline, vertical-steps connector rail). Padding stays
100% canonical.

REMAINING, not done: the deeper 'size' family work. 46 of 443 occurrences
(10.4%) are still off the canonical scale, nearly all in w-/h-. The biggest
single item is icon/icon_tile spanning 16/20/24/32/40/48/64 -- that wants one
named size ramp rather than seven raw utilities, and it is a design decision
about how many icon sizes the library should offer, not a mechanical
substitution. Suggest splitting that out rather than holding this ticket open.

title: DataTable: keyboard operability for interactive rows (a11y)
description: DataTable rows responded to click but were not keyboard-focusable, so selection and activation were pointer-only (identified while writing doc/components/data_table.md). Fix: when a table is interactive (selected_rows OR on_row_activate supplied), rows get tabindex=0 + aria-selected (valid on a <tr>'s implicit role=row), and Enter/Space mirror a click with Ctrl/Shift parity; Space preventDefaults its page-scroll. Plain display tables gain no tab stops (gated by row_is_interactive()). The internal on_row_click callback was refactored from (idx, MouseEvent) to (idx, ctrl, shift) bools so mouse and keyboard share one path. 4 unit tests on row_is_interactive; browser-verified.
close_reason: Shipped in 4e777c1 on main. Interactive rows (selected_rows or on_row_activate supplied) are focusable (tabindex=0) with aria-selected; Enter/Space mirror a click with Ctrl/Shift parity; Space preventDefaults page-scroll; plain display tables gain no tab stops. Internal on_row_click refactored (idx, MouseEvent) -> (idx, ctrl, shift) so mouse+keyboard share one path; public API unchanged. 4 unit tests on row_is_interactive() + browser-verified: selection table (Enter/Space select, Ctrl+Enter toggle 3,5, Shift+Enter extend 5,6,7, aria-selected=true on focus); activation table (Enter/Space activate count 2 no-select, Ctrl/Shift+Enter select no-activate, ArrowDown no-op); Space preventDefaulted; plain rows unfocusable; 2/22 demo tables expose tabindex, 0/18 plain tables leak one. Filed retroactively so the work has a record.

All four documented claims verified by driving real clicks: (1) plain click activates and does NOT select — count 1, selected (none); (2) Ctrl/Shift click selects and does NOT activate — count frozen at 2, set 5,6,7; (3) the index is ABSOLUTE not page-relative — page 2's first row 'User 9' reports 8, and after a descending sort 'User 12' reports 11; (4) a table WITHOUT the callback still selects on a plain click (index 2, activation count 0), confirming the 'zero behavior change by default' guarantee. title: Reusable stale-while-revalidate keyed resource cache (generalize inventory WallCache)
description: inventory-web hand-rolled an app-wide WallCache (RwSignal<Option<(key,DTO)>> in a context that survives route re-mounts): on return to a screen it renders the cached payload INSTANTLY while a background refetch revalidates (bd_4iiz-inventory-gu3; back-nav 2270ms->142ms, no spinner). This stale-while-revalidate KEYED RESOURCE CACHE is a reusable web-framework primitive — promote it so every data screen gets instant back-navigation without hand-rolling a per-screen cache. Proposed API: a use_swr_resource(key_fn, async fetcher) hook (returns cached-or-loading view state + a 'revalidating' flag) and/or a CacheProvider context keyed by a string. Keep the fetch layer pluggable (gloo-net/fetch agnostic). First consumers: inventory Lifecycle + the drilldowns (epic bd_4iiz-inventory-22t). SCOPE: web/client only — the server-side result cache (bd_4iiz-inventory-zbi) is app/server side, NOT this.
notes:
Implemented as src/utils/swr.rs (promoted alongside utils::debounce, which was extracted from the same host app for the same reason):

- SwrState<T,E> { Loading | Ready{data, revalidating} | Error } — exhaustive, so a match can't forget the cached-but-stale case an ad-hoc Option<Result<..>> match does.
- SwrCache: type-erased (Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>) so ONE app-wide context serves every screen/DTO; a key stored as one type and read as another misses rather than misrenders. get/get_untracked/set/invalidate/clear/len/is_empty.
- provide_swr_cache() / use_swr_cache() — docs stress it must go ABOVE the router (a cache inside a route dies with the route = the exact re-mount it exists to survive).
- use_swr_resource(key_fn, async fetcher) -> SwrResource { state, revalidating, key, refetch(), invalidate_and_refetch() }.
- swr_state_from(fetch, cached) — the whole decision table as a pure fn, unit-tested (10 tests) without a DOM/resource/async runtime.
- Fetch layer stays pluggable: the module never performs a request; any async Fn(String) -> Future<Output=Result<T,E>> works (gloo-net/reqwest/hand-rolled).
- Demo: new /components/swr page with a mount toggle standing in for a route re-mount, plus provide_swr_cache() above <Router> in demo main.rs.
REAL BUG caught only by driving the hook in a browser (all 8 unit tests were green through it):

On a key change, the hook rendered the PREVIOUS key's payload as if it were the new key's FRESH data, for the full fetch duration. Observed: switching to an uncached 'quarter' displayed 'payload for month (fetch #4)' labelled fresh for 1.2s, then swapped to quarter. It should have shown Loading.

Cause: a Leptos resource keeps serving its previous value while it re-runs, so after the key changes resource.get() still returns the OLD key's data. The hook trusted resource.get() as 'the fetch for the current key' — violating its own documented contract ('a value cached under the old key never renders for the new one').

Fix: the resource now resolves to (key_it_was_fetched_with, result). The state reader discards a value whose tag != the current key (treating it as 'not fetched yet' -> cache lookup -> Loading), and the cache-write Effect stores under the resource's own tag rather than key.get_untracked(), which may already have moved on. Two regression tests pin the resulting states.

Note this bug was invisible to unit tests by construction: swr_state_from's decision table was always correct — the defect was in what the hook FED it. That's the same lesson as ldui-29l: the pure math was never wrong, the DOM/reactive wiring was.

Also worth knowing: an early browser reading ('fetch #2 resolving in 16ms' despite a 1200ms simulated latency) was itself an artifact of this bug — stale values masquerading as fresh ones. After the fix, timings are a clean 1209/1214ms.

Browser-verified end-to-end: cache miss -> Loading at 4ms then fresh at 1209ms (real latency); cache hit (re-mount, standing in for back-nav) -> cached value rendered at 4ms marked 'revalidating', NEVER a spinner, revalidated to fresh at 1214ms. title: DataTable: responsive / auto-growing page size (rows-per-page from window height)
description: Consumer request from 4iiz-inventory (epic bd_4iiz-inventory-22t): pagination should GROW as the window is resized (a taller window shows more rows). Today page_size is a fixed Signal<usize> (default 10, component.rs) with no resize logic; max_height gives scroll-in-fixed-area but not a growing page size. Add opt-in responsive paging: a ResizeObserver (or window resize listener) on the table container that derives rows-per-page from available height / measured row height and feeds page_size. Lighter interim already possible (callers pass a resize-driven Signal to the existing page_size prop) — but no call site does this and the 'grows on resize' contract lives nowhere; make it a first-class opt-in prop (e.g. auto_page_size: bool). First consumer: inventory Explorer + StageDetail.
notes:
PORT SOURCE: rust-deskapp already implements this on the desktop DataTable — crates/d2d-ui/src/controls/data_table.rs: rows_per_page_for_height(h) (:675) = ((h - header_offset - PAGINATION_HEIGHT) / ROW_HEIGHT).floor().max(1); set_rows_per_page_to_fit() (:680) called on resize. Web port = a ResizeObserver on the table container feeding the SAME arithmetic into the existing page_size Signal. Not a from-scratch build — mirror the desktop logic.
Browser verification caught two defects the unit tests could not:

1. max_height is a CEILING, not a height. The container shrink-wrapped its rows, so the measured viewport was a function of the row count being derived from it -> settled at 1 row in a 382px box and could never grow. Fix: when auto_page_size is on, promote max_height to a definite 'height' (and fall back to height:100% when no max_height). The prop docs originally stated the wrong precondition ('pass max_height') and were corrected to 'needs a definite height'.

2. Infinite 2-cycle oscillation (5 rows@37px <-> 1 row@52px, forever, re-arming a timeout each pass). Root cause found from the numbers: 37+87 = 52+72 = 124 = container height. The 15px delta is a HORIZONTAL SCROLLBAR -- the wrapper is overflow-y:auto, so when the widest rendered cell makes the table wider than the wrapper, an h-scrollbar appears and is subtracted from clientHeight. That made viewport = f(row count) with no fixed point. Fix: measure with offset_height() (flex-allocated border-box height, which no scrollbar or cell content can move) instead of client_height(). A cycle-detection guard was tried first and REJECTED -- it made the ladder worse (7/9 vs 8/9) because the ResizeObserver fires multiple times per resize and the episode resets interleaved unpredictably. Removing the coupling beat patching the symptom.

Also: measurement is deferred to a 0ms macrotask (a ResizeObserver callback can run mid-layout; latching a transient left the table a row short), plus a re-measure pass keyed on page_size.

Final: resize ladder 9/9 exact vs floor((offsetH-headerH)/rowH) across grow/shrink/revisit/degenerate; degenerate 150px settles monotonically 8@52 -> 1@52 and stays (no oscillation, no churn); recovers to 5.
close_reason: Implemented: auto_page_size prop + auto_page.rs (rows_per_page_for_height, ported from d2d-ui rows_per_page_for_height). ResizeObserver on the table's scroll wrapper (mirrors toolbar's pattern) feeds the measured viewport/header/row heights into the pure fn. Web measures rendered heights rather than d2d-ui's fixed HEADER_HEIGHT/ROW_HEIGHT consts (daisyUI row height varies by table size); consts kept as fallbacks. 19 unit tests + demo section with a user-resizable box. TWO REAL BUGS found only by driving a browser (unit tests were green throughout) -- see notes.

title: AppShellIconNav: support a rail background image/pattern (brand texture behind the nav rail)
description:
GAP found while porting the 4iiz Office Performance desktop app to the web (4iiz-Office op-7hx). The desktop's branded nav rail renders a dark-navy base + a subtle vertical gradient + a cyan DOT-WAVE brand texture PNG behind the nav items. It should coexist with the existing solid-colour background (base colour + optional gradient + optional image overlay).

CONSUMER: 4iiz-Office crates/office-perf-web/src/shell.rs. Brand asset: crates/office-perf-gui/assets/brand/sidebar-bg.png (and .webp). Today the web rail is a flat navy with no texture, so it does not match the desktop.

comments.author: davidcforbes
comments.text:
Implemented on AppShellIconNav: bg_color / bg_gradient / bg_image (+ bg_size, bg_repeat).

The rail's background now stacks three layers, back to front: bg_color -> bg_gradient -> bg_image texture. All three go on the <nav>'s OWN background, and an element's background always paints beneath its content -- so nav-item hover/active backgrounds and the count badges paint on top, unobscured, with no overlay div and no z-index games. That is the 'composited UNDER the nav items, NOT tiling over hover/active states or badges' requirement, satisfied structurally.

One non-obvious finding for the consumer (4iiz-Office office-perf-web) and for the d2d-ui half of this gap:
  A bg-[#0b1e3a] CLASS does NOT reliably set the rail's base colour. The rail hard-codes bg-base-300, both are plain utilities in the same cascade layer, and the generated sheet's order decides -- measured in the browser, bg-base-300 wins and the rail stays grey. Hence bg_color is an INLINE style (inline beats any class). Use bg_color="#0b1e3a", not a bg-[...] class.

Safety: bg_image is a URL and is escaped into a quoted CSS url("...") (quotes/backslashes escaped, control chars dropped), so it cannot break out and inject declarations. bg_color is validated as colour-shaped (hex / rgb() / oklch() / var() / named / color-mix) and dropped entirely if it isn't -- 'red; background-image: url(evil)' emits nothing. bg_gradient is raw CSS by necessity (it IS a linear-gradient(...) expression) and is documented as trusted input, same trust level as the class prop.

A repeating texture wants bg_repeat="repeat" WITH bg_size="auto" (the default 'cover' scales one copy to fill the rail and defeats the tile).

Unbranded rails are untouched: with no bg_* props the component emits no style attribute at all (verified in the DOM -- 3 of the 4 rails on the demo page have no style attr).

Verified in the browser on the new demo section (/components/app-shell -> 'Branded Rail'): computed background-color = rgb(11,30,58), background-image = texture + linear-gradient, background-repeat = repeat; item labels and the '7' badge render legibly over the dot-wave. 17 app_shell unit tests incl. the injection cases.

@4iiz-Office: the interim CSS-background workaround in crates/office-perf-web/src/shell.rs can now be replaced with these props.

title: AiChat auto-scroll reads stale scroll_height, leaves latest message below fold
description: Browser smoke (ldui-0wf) confirmed the Task 19 deferred auto-scroll concern is a real bug. Repro: AiChat demo, stick engaged (scrolled to bottom), send a message. The reply arrives (bubbles 2->4, scrollHeight 352->733) but scrollTop lands at 267 while the true bottom is scrollHeight-clientHeight = 496 — ~230px of the newest content stays below the fold, and it never corrects. Also on the very first message: scrollHeight 352 vs clientHeight 237 (115px overflow) but scrollTop stays 0. Root cause: the auto-stick Effect at src/components/ai_chat/component.rs:183-191 calls el.set_scroll_top(el.scroll_height()) synchronously when  changes, but Leptos Effects run after the reactive update and BEFORE the browser lays out the newly-appended MessageBubble DOM, so scroll_height() is stale (too small). The stale programmatic scroll can also trip the on:scroll handler (component.rs:209-216) into recomputing should_stick_to_bottom with a large distance, flipping stick=false and disengaging future auto-scroll (explains scrollTop stuck at 0 on first send). Fix: defer the scroll to after paint — request_animation_frame (web_sys) before reading scroll_height and setting scroll_top, or set_timeout(0). The pure should_stick_to_bottom logic is correct and well-tested; the bug is purely the measurement timing in the Effect. NOTE: P1 theme panic (ldui-i4t) and P3 memory error (ldui-4i0) were both verified FIXED live in this same session — console is clean, no more disposal panic.
close_reason: Fixed in 3b600d4: deferred the auto-stick scroll write into a request_animation_frame callback (leptos::prelude::request_animation_frame, one-shot per Effect run, None-guarded) so it reads scroll_height AFTER the browser paints the new bubbles. Re-verified live on rebuilt WASM (a86fe2309...): after 1st message distance-from-bottom=0 (was 115px overflow at scrollTop 0); after 2nd message scrollTop 497 of 733, distance -1≈0 (was 267/dist 229 below fold). title: Integrate ui-tokens shared crate into leptos-daisyui-rs
description:
Bring in the shared `ui-tokens` crate from the Rust-DeskApp workspace so leptos-daisyui-rs consumes the same design tokens (durations, easings, shadow elevation tiers, colour palette anchors) as d2d-ui. This is the prerequisite for the motion-port epic (ldui-e1o) — without a single source of truth for motion durations and shadow tiers, every component-level port would have to redefine the same constants and the libraries would drift.

## Why now

The d2d-ui motion epic (Rust-DeskApp/beads-14f) shipped 2026-05 with a complete `ui_tokens::motion` (Easing enum, DURATION_FAST_MS/DURATION_NORMAL_MS, cubic-Bezier control points) and `ui_tokens::elevation` (LEVEL_2..LEVEL_64 Shadow structs). The motion-port epic (ldui-e1o) is parked until this anchor is in place.

## Decision: path-dep vs git-dep vs vendored

The original parity epic (beads-76r) flagged this as needing a "path-dep decision". Three options:

1. **Path-dep** (`ui-tokens = { path = "../Rust-DeskApp/crates/ui-tokens" }`) — cleanest while both repos are local. Breaks for downstream crates.io consumers and for CI without sibling-repo checkout.
2. **Git-dep** (`ui-tokens = { git = "https://github.com/davidcforbes/rust-deskapp", branch = "master" }`) — works for crates.io publication and CI. Slower (git fetch on each build). Pinning to a commit hash recommended.
3. **Vendored copy** — manual sync. Drift-prone but simple.

Recommended: git-dep with a pinned commit hash. Migrate to path-dep only for local development if needed.

## Surface to consume

From the d2d-ui ui-tokens crate (C:\dev\Rust-DeskApp\crates\ui-tokens\src\):

- `motion.rs` — `Easing { Linear, Standard, Decelerate, Accelerate }`, `DURATION_FAST_MS`, `DURATION_NORMAL_MS`, cubic-Bezier control points
- `elevation.rs` — `Shadow { offset_x, offset_y, blur, opacity }`, named tiers `LEVEL_2`/`LEVEL_4`/`LEVEL_8`/`LEVEL_16`/`LEVEL_64`
- `colour.rs` / `theme.rs` (if applicable to web) — accent + neutral palette anchors

## How web consumes these (translation strategy)

- Emit motion constants as `--ld-duration-fast: 83ms; --ld-duration-normal: 200ms;` CSS variables in a token preamble (build-time, via a small leptos-side helper).
- Easing cubic-Bezier control points emit as `cubic-bezier(...)` CSS easing functions.
- Elevation shadows emit as `box-shadow: <offset_x>px <offset_y>px <blur>px rgba(0,0,0,<opacity>);` per tier.
- Colour palette consumed via existing daisyUI theme infrastructure.

## Verification

- New crate dependency builds clean (`cargo build`, `cargo test` from leptos-daisyui-rs root).
- Token preamble CSS emitted from a small `ui_tokens_css!()` macro or build.rs.
- At least one component (Button is the obvious candidate) uses one motion token (e.g., `--ld-duration-fast` for hover transition) to prove the chain.

## Unblocks

- ldui-e1o (motion + shadow system port) — explicitly blocked-by-convention on this bead.

title: Port d2d-ui motion + shadow system to leptos-daisyui-rs
description:
Epic to port the motion + drop-shadow system shipped in the d2d-ui Rust-DeskApp workspace (beads-14f, merged 2026-05) across to leptos-daisyui-rs. Cross-stack flow:

  d2d-ui (Direct2D, native) -> leptos-daisyui-rs (Leptos/WASM, CSS) -> table-rs (sibling effort, separate epic)

## Why

d2d-ui's beads-14f epic shipped a complete motion system: eased hover/press/focus, ripple reveals, elevation lift on hover, GPU drop shadows via CLSID_D2D1Shadow, dialog scale-up + backdrop fade, toast slide-in, menu/dropdown/drawer entrances. ~70 controls migrated. The patterns are now battle-tested in native code. Bringing them to the web library accelerates app development by sharing the same visual language across renderers.

## Scope

Port these motion patterns to their CSS / Web Animations API equivalents:

- Eased state transitions (cubic-Bezier hover/press/focus opacity + scale + colour)
- Ripple click reveal (radial expanding overlay)
- Elevation lift (shadow + slight translate on hover for Card / Fab)
- Drop shadows (CSS filter: drop-shadow or box-shadow per elevation tier)
- Dialog entrance: scale 0.92 -> 1.0 + backdrop fade-in
- Toast entrance: slide-in from corner
- Menu / dropdown / drawer slide-down or edge-slide
- Focus ring animated fade-in + outset

## Source of truth (d2d-ui side)

- `crates/d2d-ui/src/motion/` -- clock, easing, transition, spring, ripple, StateAnim
- `crates/d2d-ui/src/shadow.rs` -- CLSID_D2D1Shadow wrapper + ui_tokens::elevation::Shadow
- `crates/ui-tokens/src/motion.rs` -- Easing enum + DURATION_FAST_MS / DURATION_NORMAL_MS
- `crates/ui-tokens/src/elevation.rs` -- LEVEL_2 / LEVEL_4 / LEVEL_8 / LEVEL_16 / LEVEL_64 shadow tiers
- `docs/components/motion.md` -- reference doc

## Anchor on ui-tokens (depends on ldui-wab)

This epic depends on the ui-tokens integration tracked under ldui-wab. Once leptos-daisyui-rs consumes the shared ui-tokens crate, motion durations + shadow tiers automatically stay in sync with d2d-ui via a single source of truth. Without that anchor, this port would drift.

## Suggested fan-out (children to file when work starts)

1. ui-tokens integration (already tracked: ldui-wab)
2. Eased button hover/press/focus -- the universal interaction pattern
3. Eased checkbox / toggle / radio interaction
4. Card elevation lift (LEVEL_4 -> LEVEL_8 on hover)
5. Ripple effect on click (radial overlay)
6. Dialog scale-up + backdrop fade-in
7. Toast slide-in entrance from corner
8. Menu / dropdown slide-down entrance
9. Drawer edge-slide entrance
10. Focus ring animated fade-in

## Out of scope (this epic)

- Porting to table-rs -- separate sibling epic when ready
- Wholesale rewrite of existing leptos-daisyui-rs components -- this is additive
- Reactive signal redesign -- continue using existing Leptos signal patterns

## Related

- d2d-ui WinUI 3 reference: Rust-DeskApp/beads-v3f, beads-n5a (closed 2026-05)

title: Add typed summary-row emphasis to EntityTable
description: The Office Finances snapshot has a Total row that must be visually distinct across every cell, while Contribution and other reporting snapshots have summary or aggregate rows with the same need. EntityTable has column renderers but no typed row-presentation seam, so consumers must repeat the same predicate and classes in every cell and still cannot apply one coherent row border, background, or compact treatment.
design: Prefer a narrow framework-owned semantic enum returned by a row callback, such as Standard, Summary, Muted, or Attention, rather than an unrestricted class-string hook. EntityTable owns tokens and responsive styling; consumers own only the typed classification predicate. This must remain presentation-only and must not change row identity, ordering, activation, selection, or mutation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can classify a row with a documented semantic presentation without duplicating per-cell renderers. Summary styling is coherent across wide and compact layouts, survives sorting, filtering, paging, hiding, resizing, zebra mode, hover, and focus, and remains legible in forced colors. Classification never changes row keys, accessible names, action eligibility, sort values, or source data. The default renders identically to current EntityTable. title: DataTable search input and filter selects have no accessible name
notes:
Found 2026-08-28 while converting a table in 4iiz-etl. Its style audit reports,
on EVERY page carrying a DataTable:

  COMPONENT-DRIFT  input-outside-field: input has no fieldset ancestor
    div.etl-table-region > div.w-full > div.mb-3.flex > input.input.input-bordered
  COMPONENT-DRIFT  input-outside-field: select has no fieldset ancestor
    thead > tr.data-table-filter-row > th.p-1 > select.select.select-bordered

Both elements are ldui's own: the DataTable's `searchable` input and its
per-column filter `select`. Neither sits in a `fieldset`/`Field`, and neither
carries a visible or associated label.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A LINT: a bare `input` with only a placeholder is not
labelled for a screen reader — placeholder text is not an accessible name, and
it disappears the moment someone types. The same goes for the per-column filter
selects, where "which column does this filter?" is conveyed only by physical
position in the header row.

WHAT THE CONSUMER SEES TODAY: every page that turns on `searchable` or
`filterable` costs exactly +2 drift findings, so consumers ratchet their audit
ceilings to absorb library markup they cannot fix. 4iiz-etl has now done this
twice (`schemas`, then `home`), each time recording that the added findings are
ldui's chrome rather than the page's own. That is a workaround, not a fix, and
it quietly raises the ceiling that would otherwise catch real drift.

SUGGESTED: give the search input an accessible name (visually-hidden label or
`aria-label`, ideally derived from the table's own aria-label), and give each
filter select an `aria-label` naming its column. A `fieldset`/`Field` wrapper
would satisfy the rule structurally, but the accessible name is the substance —
the rule is a proxy for it.

Not urgent for 4iiz-etl: the ceilings absorb it. Filed because the accessibility
gap is real and every consumer inherits it.

title: Charts other than BarChart/Heatmap still emit raw fill= and would hit the var()-in-presentation-attribute hazard
description: src/charts/paint.rs was introduced on 2026-08-09 (commit c153c58) to route a colour through style="fill: ..." when it contains var(), because SVG2 parses presentation attributes with the property's isolated value grammar and custom-property substitution is NOT specified to run there. Chromium already declines it for length attributes, and the SVG WG has an open request (Nov 2025) to specify or forbid it. If it is forbidden, the value stops parsing and the shape paints SOLID BLACK. Only BarChart (bar_chart.rs:129,196) and Heatmap (heatmap.rs:319) route through paint_attrs. LineChart, PieChart, StackedBarChart, StackedAreaChart and AreaChart still emit raw fill=color, so a consumer passing a daisyUI theme token (e.g. var(--color-primary)) through their color / per-segment colour props hits the same hazard with no protection.
design: Route every chart's fill through crate::charts::paint::paint_attrs, which is already value-keyed (color.contains("var(")) rather than chart-keyed, so it needs no per-chart logic. Literal colours must keep the fill attribute so existing DOM stays byte-identical - paint.rs already does this and has tests pinning it (literal_colors_keep_the_fill_attribute).
acceptance_criteria: No chart component emits a fill= attribute whose value contains var(. A test asserts this per chart. Literal-colour callers still render fill= unchanged.
notes: Raised by the fix-round re-review 2026-08-09 as an out-of-scope observation - the original finding was scoped to BarChart, so this was correctly not fixed there. Same defect class, no consumer is known to be hitting it yet.
close_reason: Landed ad52cf1. Reviewed: satisfied. Routed all 5 named charts PLUS sparkline (swept rather than working from the list), and extended paint_attrs to cover STROKE - the sharper argument being that stroke's initial value is none, so a value that stops parsing DELETES the line rather than blackening it, and LineChart/AreaChart/Sparkline draw their primary mark with stroke alone. Browser: 0 var() in any fill=/stroke= attribute vs 51 before; 71 token paints on style; 0 computing to black or none. title: Two DataTables with overlapping features: converge widgets::DataTable and components::DataTable, or document the split
description: This library ships TWO DataTable components and nothing tells a consumer which to use. components::DataTable (src/components/data_table/) is the rich one: 28 props incl. cell_renderers, typed_cells, row_class_fn, Column::action(), selection with row_key identity, column chooser, per-column filters, extra_filter, toolbar slot, auto_page_size, server-side variant. widgets::DataTable (src/widgets/data_table.rs) is a simpler Vec<Vec<String>> table but owns three things the component does NOT have: badge_column_keys, link_column_keys, and bulk_select keyed by the first cell's String id. That bead is being satisfied additively on the widget to unblock them, which deepens the duplication rather than resolving it.
design: Three options, needs the owner's call rather than an agent's: (a) port badge/link/bulk-select onto components::DataTable and deprecate the widget with a migration note; (b) keep both and document the split explicitly in CLAUDE.md and both doc comments - widget = read-mostly string tables, component = interactive typed tables; (c) reduce the widget to a thin preset over the component. (a) is the least duplication and the most migration cost for existing consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Either the two are converged, or both doc comments and CLAUDE.md state plainly which to reach for and why, so the next consumer does not pick by accident.
notes: Raised 2026-08-09 while implementing ldui-3qc. Not blocking that bead.

title: DayScheduler's hour gutter is hardcoded 12-hour AM/PM, so it stays English on a Spanish page
description:
FROM office-perf (C:/dev/4iiz-Office), found 2026-07-28 in its first Spanish UI pass.

`DayScheduler` renders the hour gutter with a hardcoded 12-hour AM/PM clock. On
a Spanish page the whole screen is Spanish and the gutter still reads:

    8 AM  9 AM  10 AM  11 AM  12 PM  1 PM  2 PM ...

Spanish-speaking locales write the 24-hour clock in this context (08:00, 13:00).
The 12-hour form exists but carries "p. m." with spaces and periods, which is
fussier than it is worth for a calendar gutter.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: office-perf's client population is ~87%
Spanish-leading, and the consumer has now made every OTHER clock on the page
language-aware — the status-bar pill, the planner's block times, My Day's
appointment times. The gutter is the only English clock left, so a single screen
shows two conventions side by side, which reads as a bug rather than as a
mixture.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, in preference order:
  1. A `hour_format: Signal<HourFormat>` (or `use_24h: Signal<bool>`) prop on
     DayScheduler, defaulting to the current 12-hour behaviour so no existing
     consumer changes.
  2. Failing that, accept a formatter closure `Fn(u32) -> String` for the
     gutter label, which keeps the locale decision entirely with the consumer.

(1) is nicer for the common case; (2) is more flexible and cannot go stale as
locales are added.

CONSUMER-SIDE WORKAROUND TODAY: none that is worth doing. office-perf renders
its own blocks INTO DayScheduler's rects but the gutter is drawn by the
component, so the only alternative is to stop using it for the backdrop — which
would give up the gridlines, now-line, overlap-lane packing and hit-testing the
component exists to provide.

NOT URGENT: the labels are readable and unambiguous, just not localised.
notes:
CORRECTION FROM office-perf, 2026-07-28 — the premise of this bead was partly WRONG, and you built on it in good faith.

I filed it saying DayScheduler "hardcodes 12-hour AM/PM". It does not, and never
did. `hour_format: Signal<HourFormat>` has been a prop since the original port
(7b34b1ff), and OFFICE-PERF was passing `HourFormat::Twelve` unconditionally.
The last English clock on our Spanish page was our own choice, and the fix was
one line on our side:

    hour_format=Signal::derive(move || match lang.get() {
        Lang::Es => HourFormat::TwentyFour,
        Lang::En => HourFormat::Twelve,
    })

Verified in the browser: Spanish now reads 08:00/09:00/10:00, English still
reads 8 AM/9 AM/10 AM.

WHAT YOU ADDED IS STILL WORTH HAVING. `hour_label` (Callback<u32, String>) is
the escape hatch for a locale that wants NEITHER convention — hour names from an
i18n catalogue, or a format neither enum arm covers. office-perf does not need
it today; a future consumer plausibly will. I would not revert it.

ONE THING WORTH FLAGGING FOR OTHER CONSUMERS: HourFormat::TwentyFour is
`#[default]`. Anyone who adopts DayScheduler WITHOUT passing `hour_format` gets
24-hour, which for an English-only app is a silent behaviour change rather than
a new capability. Might be worth a line in the component docs, or in the
changelog entry, so it is not discovered in a screenshot.

Sorry for the wasted cycle. The rule I should have followed, and now have
written down: read the component's own props before filing across a repo
boundary.
close_reason:
Shipped as an optional `hour_label: Callback<u32, String>` on both DayScheduler and WeekView (commit d1d1a5d) — the bead's option (2). Overrides `hour_format` when supplied, so a consumer can render any label it likes ("8 h", a catalogue lookup, a locale-specific 12h form).

Correction to the report's premise, which matters for the consumer: the gutter was NOT hardcoded. Option (1) has been there since the port — `hour_format: Signal<HourFormat>` defaults to `HourFormat::TwentyFour`. office-perf sees AM/PM because its day planner explicitly asks for it at office-perf-web/src/screens/day_planner.rs:1007 (`hour_format=Signal::derive(|| HourFormat::Twelve)`). So there IS a consumer-side fix available today and it is one line: make that signal read the active locale and return TwentyFour for Spanish. Nothing needs to wait on this crate.

The new closure is for the case that one-liner can't cover — a locale wanting neither 24h nor English AM/PM.

HourFormat itself is unchanged, so the port stays in step with d2d-ui's own two-variant HourFormat (crates/d2d-ui/src/controls/day_scheduler.rs:25) — the desktop face has no locale hook either.

title: TextRotate: rotating words render above the baseline and are clipped (mostly invisible)
description: User-reported (2026-07-08), confirmed LIVE on /components/text_rotate. The rotating words are almost entirely invisible/clipped: e.g. 'Hello, I'm [blank]', 'Our product is [blank] and loved by developers worldwide' — the animated word area shows nothing or a sliver. Measured live: the .text-rotate > span > span items render with their tops ~80-164px ABOVE the .text-rotate box top (all items overflowsTop:true), and the box computes overflow:hidden with height == line-height (e.g. 40px for text-4xl), so the items are positioned outside the visible band and clipped away. Even the resting first-child (opacity 1, translateY 0) is not visible. Root cause is the component's positioning model in demo/custom-components.css lines 139-161: .text-rotate (relative, inline-block), middle .text-rotate>span (relative, inline-block, no height), items .text-rotate>span>span (absolute, top:0 left:0). The absolute items are not aligned to the text baseline and the container does not establish a correct visible band, so with the translateY(0 -> -20px) keyframes the text renders above the line. NOTE: source .text-rotate rule sets NO overflow, yet it computes overflow:hidden — track down where that comes from (possibly a Tailwind utility or inherited rule) as part of the fix. FIX (needs iterative CSS rework, not a one-liner): rebuild the container as a fixed-height overflow-hidden band with items vertically stacked and animating within it, aligned to baseline; verify each of the 6 demo examples shows the rotating word fully. Component: src/components/text_rotate/component.rs (markup) + demo/custom-components.css (.text-rotate rules + text-rotate-N-items keyframes). P3 visual.
close_reason: Fixed in 67f768e. Rewrote .text-rotate CSS (demo/custom-components.css) from a broken absolute/relative model to an inline-grid stack: display:contents on the middle span flattens it so items become grid children of .text-rotate, all sharing grid cell 1/1 (overlap in place), box sizes to widest word, visible word sits on the text baseline. Root cause was the old middle container computing to ~3 line-heights (120px), pushing items ~80px above the visible band where overflow clipped them. Verified live on the rebuilt artifact across all 6 demo examples: every visible word visInBand:true + box alignedToLine:true; animation cycles one word at a time correctly.

title: Hover3d: flicker on hover + cards overlap section headers
description:
User-reported (2026-07-08), two bugs on the Hover 3D demo page, both rooted in demo/custom-components.css .hover-3d (lines 256-284) + src/components/hover_3d/component.rs.

ISSUE 1 — FLICKER while hovering (even mouse ~stationary). Diagnosed LIVE with event counters: with a truly stationary cursor, ZERO mouse events fire over 2s and transform stays flat, and during movement each mousemove produces exactly one clean transform write (no cascade). So it is NOT a JS mousemove/mouseleave feedback loop. Root cause is GPU 3D compositing / z-fighting: .hover-3d sets transform-style:preserve-3d + perspective:1000px (lines 258-259) and hosts 8 empty hover-zone divs at z-index:10, pointer-events:all (lines 269-275) that are COPLANAR in that same 3D context with the tilted content child; the content also has transition:transform 0.1s (line 265). Once any tilt is applied (any hover), the coplanar zone overlay and the perspective-projected card surface z-fight and the compositor repaints every frame = visible flicker. Real-mouse micro-jitter + the 0.1s transition adds a jello wobble on top.
FIX options (pick minimal): (a) take the hover content out of coplanar conflict / promote it to its own layer — e.g. give the content will-change:transform or translateZ(0), or wrap the tilt target in an inner element isolated from the zones; (b) set pointer-events:none on the tilting content so only the (non-moving) zones+host do hit-testing; (c) drop transform-style:preserve-3d on the content children (they have no 3D children) and/or remove the 0.1s transition so tilt is instant. Verify live that flicker stops.

ISSUE 2 — cards OVERLAP the section header above them. Measured LIVE (static, NOT tilt-related — max up-tilt moves card only ~1px): the .hover-3d host box is SHORTER than its card content and centers the overflow, so the card bleeds ~10-22px ABOVE the host top into the preceding h2. E.g. Credit Card host height 224px vs card content 269px -> card top 22px above host; card top 382 vs 'Credit Card Style' h2 bottom 388 = 6px overlap; Product Showcase cards 11px over their h2. Host computes display:grid with a track shorter than content (source not in the .hover-3d rule as read — implementer should pin where display:grid/height comes from: a Tailwind class, the Card, or an inherited rule). FIX: make .hover-3d size to its content (height:auto / min-content, or align/justify so the card doesn't overflow the track), OR add adequate top spacing so the 3D card cannot collide with the header. Verify the card no longer touches the h2 above at rest.

Both fixes land in demo/custom-components.css and possibly src/components/hover_3d/component.rs. Low priority visual polish, but user-visible. NOTE during repro the MCP browser tab kept auto-drifting between hover_3d/hover_gallery/icon_tile — that was tooling confusion with multiple tabs, not a product routing bug (hover_3d loads fine on direct nav).
close_reason: Fixed in 5716a32 (demo/custom-components.css). OVERLAP: verified FIXED (measured + visual on rebuilt artifact). The perspective-projected card rendered ~10-27px outside its host box and collided with the section header above; added margin-block:1.5rem so the tilt has breathing room — card-top-to-header gaps went from -6..-11px (overlapping) to +13..+18px (clear); confirmed visually (Basic/Credit Card/Product Showcase all have clear space below their headers). FLICKER: changed the tilted content from transform-style:preserve-3d to flat — it removes the content from a shared 3D context coplanar with the z-index:10 hover-zone overlay (the diagnosed GPU z-fighting/repaint cause) while the tilt still works (verified: rotateX/Y still renders as matrix3d via the host's inherited perspective). CAVEAT: the flicker is a compositing repaint that only manifests with real-mouse hover (0 JS events fire on a stationary CDP cursor), so I could not reproduce it headlessly to confirm the fix eliminates it — needs user confirmation with a real mouse; reopen if it persists.
